### 5.16 Spatial matcher and PathMap-native retry PDA [SS-A10]

#### 5.16.1 The defect

The recursive `SpatialMatcherContext` component crossed `Par`, `Expr`, binder records, ordered and
unordered collections, connectives, and EPathMap values. A free-variable pattern forced the semantic
path and measured approximately **70,237 B/level in debug** before conversion; a concrete pattern could
bypass that path and therefore was not a valid witness by itself. The same component contained two
additional depth/width mechanisms: concrete `Receive`/`New` matching re-entered through `match_pars`, and
subset search recursively retried candidate pairings while carrying mutable binding state.

Flattening EPathMap would have hidden rather than repaired the defect. Set mode is `PathMap<()>`, map
mode is `PathMap<Par>`, and prefix topology, algebra, zipper navigation, and compact ACTree03 storage are
part of the representation. A `Vec<Par>` or hash collection would discard those properties and add
allocation before matching began.

#### 5.16.2 Architecture of the repair

Commits `78611b11`, `6799b406`, and `fc497f94` compile the complete heterogeneous matcher dependency
component into one explicit machine. Work items represent target/pattern pairs, result reductions,
collection cursors, connective snapshots, and retry continuations. A `FreeMap` snapshot belongs to the
frame that may roll back: failed disjunction alternatives, negation, and augmenting-path retries restore
their entry state; successful sequential/conjunctive children commit in source order.

EPathMap matching remains trie-native. Exact set/map members are removed with PathMap subtraction before
dynamic matching. Set entries stream as owned byte keys from `PathMap<()>`; map entries stream as owned
key/value pairs from `PathMap<Par>`. The singleton fast path (`98bb3d5e`) removes the sole pair through
owned zippers and moves the `Par` value directly into the matcher PDA. Larger ambiguous sets retain the
general retry-capable augmenting machine. No PathMap crate change, list projection, or mixed set/map
carrier was introduced.

Commit `714d618c` closes the memory-layout residual without changing the abstract machine. Large
heterogeneous states are boxed at the `Job`/`Frame` boundary, reducing the two contiguous enum slots
from **1,504 / 1,112 bytes to 64 / 64 bytes**. A unit test makes those ceilings executable. For the
singleton `PathMap<Par>` shape, a concrete key is compared in its canonical encoded PathMap form and
the PDA descends directly into the dynamic value; only a connective-bearing key is decoded and spatially
matched. This is a trie specialization, not a list projection, and the general ambiguous-key retry
machine remains available.

Commit `6f1412ee` removes the remaining singleton preflight lookup and redundant pattern-key decode.
Every exact singleton is moved through the owned PathMap entry stream: concrete `PathMap<()>` members
compare their canonical key bytes; concrete `PathMap<Par>` keys compare those bytes and concrete values
compare directly; only connective-bearing keys or values enter the matcher PDA. Empty remains the
neutral `EPathMapRepr::Empty` state until the first set or map insertion selects a homogeneous mode.
The recursive-oracle corpus now pins empty behavior and concrete singleton set/map equality plus key and
value refusal. No entry projection or PathMap crate change is involved.

#### 5.16.3 Results

All stack commands used one Cargo job, zero swap, and a systemd RSS ceiling. **MEASURED**:

| subject | axis and ladder | debug minimum stack | release minimum stack | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `spatial_binding` | depth 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 4,096 | about 80 KiB at both ends | about 36 KiB at both ends | **0 B/level**; free binding committed |
| `spatial_concrete_binders` | depth 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 4,096 | about 88 KiB at both ends | about 32 KiB at both ends | **0 B/level**; concrete binder path reached |
| `spatial_epathmap_map_depth` | depth 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 4,096 | 72 KiB at both ends | 28 KiB at both ends | **0 B/level**; deepest map value binds |
| `spatial_epathmap_set_wide` | width 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 65,536 | 164 KiB at both ends | 92 KiB at both ends | **0 B/member**; `PathMap<()>` specialization |
| `spatial_epathmap_map_wide` | width 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 65,536 | 80 KiB at both ends | 36 KiB at both ends | **0 B/member**; `PathMap<Par>` specialization |

The complete matcher-inclusive register is **45 converted subjects = 37 depth + 8 width**, with empty
production tripwire lists. Post-layout full debug/release gate runs completed in **172.07 s / 26.30 s**.
Final `6f1412ee` revalidation completed with the same **8/8 active, 4 intentionally ignored** result in
**200.40 s / 26.83 s** debug/release; elapsed variation is not used as a performance claim.
The initially correct but clone-heavy nested map witness took **97.29 s** at depth 4,096 in debug;
moving the singleton value through the owned zipper reduced it to **0.31 s** (about **314×**) without
specializing away the general retry path.

The bounded recursive oracle under `rholang/tests/support/spatial_matcher_oracle` compares both verdict
and final `FreeMap`; the corpus now executes 32 explicit target/pattern comparisons, including the six
empty/concrete-singleton additions. The generated boundary manifest
passes **5/5**. Rocq's admission-free `spatial_match_pda_equivalent_to_recursive_match` instantiates the
generic PDA theorem with state transformers and separately proves binding consistency/conflict, ordered
retry, negation isolation, and singleton ownership equivalence. The independent TLA+ matcher model
explores **607 generated / 478 distinct states** to depth 4 without error; the generic model explores
**3,238 generated / 2,816 distinct states** to depth 8.

#### 5.16.4 Complexity, allocation, and residuals

Native stack is $`O(1)`$ in match depth and candidate width. Explicit control storage is
$`O(d + w + r)`$ in the live depth, collection frontier, and retry frontier; candidate enumeration is
necessarily data-dependent, but exact PathMap subtraction and singleton moves avoid manufacturing a
dense bipartite problem for the common shapes. The measured 314× singleton improvement establishes the
dominant clone removal.

The previously missing allocator/RSS measurement is now closed with a matched fixture-only control.
Both processes construct and validate the same nested `PathMap<Par>` target/pattern pair; only the
subject enters the matcher. Heaptrack and `/usr/bin/time -v` ran at depths 512 and 4,096 in release,
one Cargo job, `MemoryMax=9G`, and zero swap. Raw rows are versioned in
[`measurements/spatial-matcher-heap-2026-08-04.tsv`](measurements/spatial-matcher-heap-2026-08-04.tsv).
Heap columns below preserve heaptrack's own `M` display unit; RSS columns are the exact KiB emitted by
GNU `time`.

| metric | before `714d618c` | after `714d618c` | final `6f1412ee` | result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| matcher-minus-control allocation calls, depth 512 / 4,096 | 17,434 / 139,293 | 15,384 / 122,907 | 11,288 / 90,139 | slope **34.001 $`\rightarrow`$ 30.001 $`\rightarrow`$ 22.001 calls/level** |
| matcher-minus-control temporary allocations, depth 512 / 4,096 | 2,561 / 20,481 | 1,537 / 12,289 | 1,025 / 8,193 | slope **5.000 $`\rightarrow`$ 3.000 $`\rightarrow`$ 2.000 calls/level** |
| heaptrack peak heap, subject / control at 512 | 11.58 / 1.03 M | 1.03 / 1.03 M | 1.03 / 1.03 M | matcher does not raise the fixture peak |
| heaptrack peak heap, subject / control at 4,096 | 91.98 / 7.63 M | 7.63 / 7.63 M | 7.63 / 7.63 M | matcher does not raise the fixture peak |
| unprofiled maximum RSS, subject at 512 / 4,096 | 23,452 / 79,676 KiB | 23,276 / 23,240 KiB | 23,016 / 23,024 KiB | positive RSS slope eliminated |
| unprofiled matcher-minus-control RSS, 512 / 4,096 | 628 / 56,780 KiB | 608 / 40 KiB | -536 / 48 KiB | no positive retained-work-stack slope; endpoint differences are process noise |
| heaptrack runtime, depth 4,096 | 0.332 s | 0.097 s | 0.088 s | **3.77× faster than the pre-layout run** |

The post-change negative fitted RSS difference is allocator/process noise, not a claim that deeper
matching releases memory. The scientifically supported claim is narrower: subject RSS is flat across
the ladder, the matched control sets the heap peak, and no positive retained-work-stack slope is visible.
Allocation counts remain linear because every trie level must still be visited and decoded; the change
removes oversized *live capacity*, not the necessary $`\Theta(d)`$ traversal work.

Within the audited matcher component, no production recursive traversal remains. The recursive oracle is
test-only and shallow-bounded. The strengthened source census keys functions by file, name, and source
offset so overloaded impl methods cannot overwrite each other; its current exact-set result is **566**
recursive components, **41** term-family components across **24** files, **18** mutual components, and
zero unmeasured dispositions. No `RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, traversal-depth limit, or PathMap fork is
part of the repair.

#### 5.16.5 RSpace candidate selection and enumeration PDA [SS-A11]

##### 5.16.5.1 The defect

The RSpace commit selector filled a receive's binds with a recursive depth-first search in
`rspace++/src/rspace/space_matcher.rs`. The enabled-rendezvous query contained a second recursive copy
of the same search. **DERIVED:** each descent filled exactly one bind, so a receive with $`b`$ binds
consumed $`\Theta(b)`$ native call frames even when every channel held one datum and the search itself
was linear. Receive arity is controlled by source text; it has no trustworthy native-stack bound.
The duplicated selector/enumerator walks also made candidate ordering, residual-pool rollback, and
guard consultation two implementations of one consensus-visible rule.

##### 5.16.5.2 Architecture of the repair, and why this shape

One explicit-frame PDA now owns both modes. Its states are `Descend`, `Scan`, and `Return`; a frame
stores the current channel/pattern pair, a resumable `CandidateScan`, an optional reserved position,
and whether any complete leaf reached the guard. `CandidateScan::All` stores the next canonical
position; `CandidateScan::Indexed` stores a sorted fixed-width position slice and its next index.
The scan is constructed once when the frame is entered rather than rebuilding a prefix query at
each retry. The selector supplies a leaf callback
that stops at the first admissible selection. The enumerator supplies a callback that clones the
accepted selection and continues. Thus the enumeration head is the selector result by construction,
not by coordination between sibling algorithms.

Each channel has one `CandidatePool`: a copy-on-write `PathMap<Multiplicity>` Bag subtrie is the
immutable selection authority, and a separate initially empty `PathMap<Multiplicity>` Bag records
only speculative nonpersistent demand. A derived `CandidateCatalog` shares canonical order and one
lazy decode cell per distinct trie key across pool snapshots. A catalog-local
`PathMap<CandidatePosition>` maps each complete relative RhoPathV1 key to a fixed-width `u64`
position. That one trie serves known-path membership for persistent zero-to-one reactivation and
indexed structural-prefix scans; no duplicate `PathMap<()>` and no platform-width trie value remain.
It is constructed once with the catalog, refreshed after permanent membership changes, and never
substitutes for the `PathMap<Multiplicity>` authority. The chosen-candidate stack and reservation
Bag obey the transaction law: an accepted early stop leaves nonpersistent demand recorded; an
exhausted subtree removes its parent's demand; exhaustive enumeration restores the entry state.
The authority is never decremented by selection, and persistent records never enter the reservation
Bag. A `Vec<Par>`, expanded occurrence list, per-frame pool clone, traversal-depth cap,
enlarged `RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, and a second enumerator were rejected.

##### 5.16.5.3 How the fix was made

The former `search_candidate_selection` and `enumerate_admissible_selections` recursive bodies were
replaced by calls to private `walk_candidate_selections`. The machine preserves pool order, advances a
parent cursor only after the selected child returns, and emits the pre-existing
`GuardRejected`/`NoSpatialMatch` backtrack counters at the same return boundary. Refinement
`5329b27a3` removes expanded datum pools and per-frame residual copies: descent originally
decremented the channel-local Bag, return incremented it, and accepted candidates carried either an
exact stored trie path or the distinct `Fresh` address. Firing removes exact paths, so same-channel
batches cannot shift one another. `173bf4e07` then separates that overloaded residual into immutable
authority plus a multiplicity-aware reservation Bag: descent increments demand, return decrements
demand, and exact cardinality makes the empty test constant-time without the public `u64` saturation
boundary. `2eb0d3871` shares the canonical catalog and decode cells across pool construction;
`d50b1183d` encodes the channel prefix once and holds one loaded-store read lock across the hot
PathMap lookup. Retained-automaton checkpoints `a89cbc294`, `f149cef2b`, and `ea8c39f92` add one
`PathMap<TerminalId>` transition segment per receive-bind position. `TerminalId` and `CandidateId`
are fixed-width `u64` newtypes; an append-only linked terminal arena represents multiple candidates
at one path without reference-counting primitive identifiers. The terminal identifier uses a
nonzero one-based encoding, so an optional predecessor occupies one 64-bit word and each arena node
is two fixed-width words. A lookup descends the fresh datum path
with an iterative read zipper and marks terminals at each visited prefix; non-indexable
patterns live at the root and therefore cannot be pruned. The automaton cache is sharded by channel
group, versioned independently per group, invalidated by whole-store generation changes, and
borrowed during lookup rather than cloned. Counter saturation disables the derived cache instead of
introducing a correctness or traversal limit. No event hash, serialized record, PathMap crate code,
or cost-accounting rule changed.

Checkpoint `564dac0b4` adds the complementary resting-data exact-ground slice. A matcher opts in only
when its retained pattern and datum paths satisfy the RhoPath prefix-superset contract. The PDA then
uses a borrowed read zipper at the framed structural prefix to collect catalog positions, sorts
those positions to restore canonical selection order, and resumes through `CandidateScan::Indexed`.
Unsupported matchers and patterns use `CandidateScan::All`. The Bag is checked before reservation,
fresh data is checked through its retained path, and the spatial matcher remains the final oracle;
therefore a prefix false positive costs work but cannot become an accepted match.

Checkpoint `f43858ec2` replaces the one-sided prefix cut with a synchronized receive-first product
cursor. One borrowed read zipper remains on the authoritative `PathMap<Multiplicity>` Bag while a
second remains on the derived `PathMap<CandidatePosition>` structural index. Exact transitions move
both zippers together; wildcard transitions enumerate the intersection of their child masks; a
candidate position is emitted only when both terminal values exist. The iterative query scanner
validates both framing layers and escaped zeros, and a `PathMap` capture environment enforces
repeated-variable equality without a hash-table or expanded-term authority. The compiled fragment
at that checkpoint included exact whole terms, whole-term wildcard/free-variable captures, repeated
captures, and ordered list remainder. Unsupported nested schema arms still took the canonical full
scan. This is a Bag/position-index product for receive-first lookup, not the separately required
retained-automaton/Bag product for datum-first lookup.

Checkpoint `71d378e73` supplies the generated schema traversal boundary for the next conversion.
The existing descriptor pass now emits one ascending-tag `RhoMatchProgram` and exhaustive
`ParCursor` accessor per message, with typed scalar, optional, sequence, map, and oneof values.
`RhoPathCursor` advances those values with an explicit heap worklist. The small-stack gate traverses
20,000 nested EList nodes and 20,000 siblings on a 256 KiB worker stack. EPathMap is not interpreted
as a message sequence: the cursor yields the borrowed EPathMap once for native PathMap zipper/PDA
delegation, and a cold snapshot remains cold before and after the walk. No RSpace caller uses this
cursor yet, so the checkpoint changes no match verdict or COMM and does not close the still-open
nested-instruction or retained-automaton/Bag-product obligations.

Checkpoints `155ecdf54` and `d858058d4` activate the generated cursor as the datum-side and exact
receive-pattern structural encoder. `RMP1` is emitted in one pass from the heap worklist; an
incremental outer framer consumes each completed top-level term immediately instead of retaining a
`Vec<Vec<u8>>`. EPathMap contributes mode, cardinality, and a domain-separated BLAKE2b-256 digest
computed by an iterative read-zipper depth-first walk. That walk visits each logical trie edge once,
stores only the heap traversal frontier, does not include map values, and never forces
`trie_snapshot()`. Omitting values is conservative because this digest can only prune candidates;
the native EPathMap/spatial matcher decides acceptance. The architecture-dependent
`PathMap::hash` is not used. Exact and whole-term query paths are live; nested binding instructions
and associative-commutative residual execution remain open.

Checkpoint `edd166671` adds a zero-copy `RMP1` token cursor and descriptor-exact validator. Message
dispatch indexes the generated registry in constant time; generated field metadata carries child
type identifiers and complete oneof tag/payload schemas. Validation is a single forward token pass
whose nested control resides in a heap `Vec<ValidationFrame>`. Subtree extent discovery is a second
iterative scan from a validated token boundary with a heap closer stack. Neither path recursively
calls itself, reconstructs `Par`, forces an EPathMap snapshot, sets `RUST_MIN_STACK`, uses
`stacker`, or imposes an input depth/width cap. The focused byte-cursor suite passes **3/3** in
**0.67 seconds** and the generated-schema suite passes **4/4** in **0.28 seconds**; the former
includes validation and deepest-subtree navigation through a 20,000-level term on a 256 KiB worker
stack. These are test-harness elapsed times under a 5 GiB zero-swap cap, not standalone RSS
measurements.

Checkpoint `bbdd22887` adds the lossless inverse at the token layer. A validated path iterates its
borrowed typed tokens and re-emits canonical **Rholang Match Path format version 1 (RMP1)** bytes
into one output buffer; it never rebuilds a
recursive `Par`. This boundary is deliberate because the EPathMap token contains a
domain-separated key-topology digest and is not an invertible serialization of map values. The
complete 66-shape descriptor corpus now passes encode/validate/token-re-encode byte identity, and a
committed manifest pins every encoded length and BLAKE2b-256 digest independently of host pointer
width. The 20,000-level re-encode also passes on the existing 256 KiB worker stack. Focused
`match_path_cursor` tests pass **6/6**, and strict Clippy for the library and target passes under an
8 GiB zero-swap scope. This closes the codec round-trip and cross-platform-byte gaps without a
native-stack slope, `RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, or an artificial traversal bound.

Checkpoint `b6b53d1b3` activates an ordered nested-query PDA without decoding `Par`. The compiler
reuses the generated event encoder to divide an EList or ETuple pattern into exact RMP1 byte runs and
whole-`Par` capture or wildcard instructions. Unsupported unordered, associative-commutative,
remainder-bearing, connective, or otherwise unrecognized shapes fail closed to the existing spatial
scan. At execution, the first exact instruction run is escaped twice and descended directly through
the synchronized Bag/position PathMap product. Wildcards and captures use an explicit heap closer
stack to consume one self-delimiting RMP1 subvalue; repeated captures compare canonical escaped
slices. The same machine handles once-escaped in-memory structure frames and twice-escaped stored
product frames through explicit modes rather than format guessing.

The focused framing suite passes **9/9**, including rejection of every tested shallow token
truncation and a
20,000-level nested value on a 128 KiB worker stack. The production product suite passes **8/8**; a
zero-heavy 256-candidate nested differential preserves the control result while reducing calls into
the spatial matcher from 256 to 1. Focused `rspace_plus_plus` and `models` strict lint and the
production `rholang` library strict lint pass. The aggregate Rholang `mod` test lint remains blocked
by 70 pre-existing `useless_vec` findings in unrelated legacy tests. No standalone RSS or comparative
latency result is inferred from these executable gates.

Checkpoint `e1a587c9f` reuses that stack-safe query machine in the datum-first retained automaton.
Each waiting pattern is stored at its longest exact structural prefix in the existing
`PathMap<TerminalId>` segment. The iterative zipper walk reaches only terminals on the fresh datum's
prefix chain; a residual query then validates wildcard/capture structure on borrowed canonical bytes
before the spatial matcher. Unsupported patterns remain root terminals. There is no fresh-datum Bag,
query-trie clone, recursive traversal, or decoded `Par` projection. The combined production pruning
suite passes **9/9**; its canonically last 256-receive witness preserves the COMM result, event trace,
and post-state map while reducing spatial calls from 256 to 1. Focused strict lint passes. Resource
slopes and the expanded benchmark matrix remain open and are not inferred from test elapsed time.

Checkpoint `5a56376b4` adds the retained-filter composition proof to `SpatialMatcher.v`. It models
the production filter as the conjunction of an exact-prefix predicate and a residual-query
predicate for eligible patterns, with root fallback represented by unconditional retention. From
the two local superset obligations—every successful spatial match accepts both predicates—it proves
that filtering has no false negatives and preserves the first spatially accepted candidate in the
predecessor's canonical list order. The complete bounded proof bundle passes: all four Rocq
theories, Verus `--no-cheating` (**6/6**), Z3, the PDA TLC model (**3,238 generated / 2,816 distinct
states**), and the spatial-matcher TLC model (**607 generated / 478 distinct states**). This closes
the abstract composition law only. The generated Rust compiler must still discharge both premises
over every eligible schema family; unordered/multiplicity-aware matching and generated schedule
replay remain open. Consequently, no consensus-equivalence or final resource conclusion is inferred
from the theorem alone.

Checkpoint `697db373b` discharges the variant-specific portion of the ordered compiler boundary.
`compile_ordered_nested_query` consumes the already-generated `RhoPathCursor` for all 16 ordered
binary expression variants, ordered unary expressions, `EMatches`, methods, lists, and tuples. The
same explicit byte-query PDA executes every resulting program; no variant adds native recursion,
decoded-term materialization, or a traversal limit. One `PathMap<()>` capture registry spans all
top-level atoms and nested holes. A repeated Rholang free-variable level rejects the derived query
because the legacy spatial matcher accumulates nonlinear occurrences rather than imposing generic
RhoPath equality. Associative-commutative carriers remain on the separate open workstream. The
focused compiler suite passes **11/11**, the complete matcher group passes **61/61**, and the three
RSpace product/automaton/path suites pass **22/22**; formatting and strict production-library lint
also pass. These are functional and stack-architecture gates, not new RSS or throughput samples.

Checkpoint `5f768e7ce` closes the concrete no-false-negative premise for the supported generated
compiler slice. `SpatialMatcher.v` models exact, hole, and ordered RMP1 compilation and proves that
every spatial success is accepted by the compiled query; unsupported patterns have no compilation
derivation and therefore retain the production fallback. The executable differential observes all
**58** generated root programs, checks exact identity queries for every visited node, and subjects
every successful case in the independent recursive-oracle corpus to the production compiler. The
matcher group passes **23/23**, the formal manifest and RMP1 cursor suites pass **12/12**, and Rocq
kernel checking succeeds under a 4 GiB / zero-swap cap. This is a semantic and constant-native-stack
result; it adds no benchmark sample and does not close AC compilation or generated play/replay.

Checkpoint `304dc13e9` supplies the missing generated play/replay schedule for the supported ordered
slice. Each of the 21 eligible expression families drives the real control and PathMap-indexed
RSpaces through two negative data, a waiting receive, and one matching datum. Play results, event
histories, stores, and checkpoint roots agree; rigged replay reproduces the play roots and exhausts
the replay data. The complete focused retained-path module passes **12/12** under an 8 GiB,
zero-swap scope. The test adds no native recursion, artificial traversal bound, or benchmark sample.
Associative-commutative compilation and generated schedules remain open.

Checkpoint `250e96c80` adds a PathMap-native candidate domain in front of the already-iterative
`ListMachine` augmenting-path PDA. Each compatible unordered target is encoded through the shared
RMP1 structural sequence and inserted into `PathMap<ListTargetId>`. Its fixed-width nonzero `u64`
payload names a node in one flat collision arena; candidate domains are owned boxed `u64` arrays,
not reference-counted platform-width primitives or per-trie-node vectors. Generated exact or
ordered nested queries cut the trie, query matches reject false structural candidates, and original
target-position sorting restores the predecessor's search order before the existing PDA runs.
Unsupported, nonselective, and nonlinear patterns use the full domain. The spatial matcher remains
the verdict authority, so value-insensitive EPathMap structural hashes can only add work.

At width 128, exact diagonal matching falls from the frozen nominal **8,256** spatial edge
evaluations to **128**. An ordered-nested ESet witness likewise performs **128** successful edges
and agrees with the recursive oracle. The unchanged 51-sample displacement control remains
exhaustive at **16,257** treatment edges versus **699,263** nominal calls in every sample. Its
isolated process completes in **56.90 s** and peaks at **100.8 MiB RSS** under a 4 GiB zero-swap
scope. These deterministic edge and resource observations are not a latency or throughput
comparison. The complete matcher-library group passes **53/53**, the affected RSpace
query/product/automaton group passes **22/22**, and strict production lint passes. Live consumption
of multiplicity deltas, constrained-first dynamic AC search, EPathMap-native lattice/algebra
integration, small-stack search-width measurement, and formal completeness remain open.

Checkpoint `2d91c4394` makes that inner-AC catalog multiplicity-authoritative. Each supported target
is keyed by one complete channel-relative RhoPath: the framed RMP1 structural sequence is the trie
prefix and a generated, stack-safe canonical-bincode sequence is the injective identity suffix.
Equal values therefore occupy one `Bag` (`PathMap<Multiplicity>`) cell; a parallel nonzero `u64`
group identifier reaches original positions only when predecessor ordering must be reconstructed.
Final ESet/EMap remainders are computed as the native Bag difference between the target Bag and
term-consumed Bag, then materialized in predecessor order. The recursive oracle agrees on the new
residual case; RhoPath framing is 10/10, the focused matcher-library group is 17/17, compile and
strict production lint pass under 8 GiB/zero-swap scopes. No native recursion, depth cap,
`RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, platform-width trie payload, or reference-counted primitive is added.
Competing host `rustc` processes made this an invalid benchmark window, so no latency, throughput,
or new RSS comparison is inferred. Search-time consumption of Bag assignment/reservation deltas and
the concrete compiler superset proof remained open at that checkpoint.

Checkpoint `bbe91b90f` makes the generated candidate catalog total across the unordered `Par` field
families. `Send`, `Receive`, `New`, `Expr`, `Match`, `Bundle`, `GUnforgeable`, and `ReceiveBind`
roots use the same iterative RMP1 cursor and the reused one-walk canonical-bincode encoder as
`Par`/map-entry roots. The compiler declines a dynamic `Receive` query because its bind sequence is
AC even though protobuf stores it in an ordered vector; this is a deliberate no-false-negative
fallback. A 128-send differential performs exactly 128 successful spatial edges rather than the
16,384 Cartesian pairs and returns the recursive oracle's 128 bindings. The complete focused
matcher group passes **18/18**, and strict production lint passes.

Checkpoint `3a70ddc58` makes visitation of byte-identical targets multiplicity-native inside the
augmenting-path PDA. The seen-target state for a true multiset is a `Bag`; the count for an identity
is the visited prefix of that group's predecessor-order positions, and every update is checked to
remain a subbag of the target. Set-shaped all-distinct targets retain one bit per position because
there is no multiplicity to compress and a PathMap lookup on every rejected edge would add work.
The existing three-element permutation/duplicate/nonlinearity differential and the semantic corpus,
including the three-identical-send remainder, pass without changing the 51-sample edge schedule.
An initial all-target Bag treatment took **120.59 s** in a debug control versus an earlier
approximately **58 s** run, but a competing multi-core pgmcp test and several other `rustc`
processes make that wall time scientifically invalid. The implementation nevertheless removed that
unnecessary all-distinct trie lane on structural grounds. No throughput, RSS, or allocation claim
is made until an uncontended release experiment compares the duplicate lane.

Checkpoint `ad5d37a59` removes repeated structural and canonical-bincode walks for adjacent
byte-identical normalized targets. The equality gate is the generated stack-safe total order, whose
comparison includes `locally_free` metadata; Rholang's metadata-insensitive `PartialEq` is not used.
A 64-occurrence duplicate control records one target-key encoding, whereas values that differ only
in metadata retain two identities. No recursive traversal, auxiliary stack, or traversal cap is
introduced.

Checkpoint `26b72b096` removes the `T-P` occurrence-expanded universal remainder vertices from the
associative-commutative matching graph. It seeds their predecessor-equivalent occupancy in one
linear pass and quotient-compresses their identity into a single `Remainder` assignment kind. If a
real term displaces an occupant, one explicit heap-PDA cursor restarts the same locally-free target
scan that the displaced filler root formerly performed. Search backtracking, pending assignments,
and displacement chains remain heap state; native call depth is independent of target and pattern
width. Final remainder multiplicities are the authoritative target Bag minus the term-consumed Bag,
with original positions retained solely as deterministic witnesses. No `RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`,
alternate stack, or depth/width limit is used.

The width-128 remainder witness evaluates one real edge and captures the other 127 sends rather than
constructing a dense filler relation. Full verdict and `FreeMap` equality with the frozen recursive
oracle holds for all 651 binary target/pattern sequences through width four and for the
locally-free refusal edge case. The complete spatial differential module passes 12/12, five
affected matcher integration suites pass 81/81, and strict production-library lint passes. These
are stack architecture, semantic, and deterministic-work results. They are not a release latency,
allocation, or RSS comparison; that resource evidence remains open.

Pgmcp experiment 246 subsequently tested one precise search-time reservation design. The control
kept the predecessor's allocation-free augmenting-path assignment writes and scanned final
assignments once to build the term-consumed Bag. The treatment updated a normalized `BagDelta`
only while unwinding a complete, already-successful augmenting root; speculative edges never
mutated it. A displacement witness recorded three additions, one cancellation removal, and final
cardinality two, while the complete focused differential passed **14/14**, including all **651**
bounded oracle cases. The one-shot CPU-8 Criterion run used 82 samples per arm at 16, 256, and
4,096 targets under 8 GiB and zero swap. At the 4,096-target primary, the mean changed from
**80.921 ms** to **80.623 ms**, an improvement of only **0.369%**; Welch's one-sided p-value was
**0.09776**, Cohen's effect size was $`-0.203`$, and the 95% treatment-minus-control interval
**[-0.751 ms, 0.155 ms]** cross zero. The 16-target cell regressed **2.140%** and the 256-target
cell improved **1.269%**. This fails the preregistered primary requirement of at least 5% and is
rejected. Checkpoint `facfedf15` preserves the exact falsified implementation; `eb5d4c580`
restores the measured control, whose postflight passes **13/13** plus strict production-library
Clippy. No stack-safety or consensus claim depends on the rejected treatment.

Checkpoint `0d7a6a3f8` supplies the standalone Bag transaction primitive required by that open
search integration. A normalized `BagDelta` records exact-key additions and removals, validates the
whole transition before mutation, and applies or reverts without partially changing the trie on
overflow or underflow. Checkpoint `1560f4371` then serializes the Bag as the canonical raw ACTree03
arena of its authoritative `PathMap<Multiplicity>`. A shared iterative reader validates canonical
topology and streams zero-copy compressed-line key ranges; EPathMap now uses the same physical
reader without sharing Bag value semantics or projecting entries into a vector.

The compact-image gate round-trips one 200,000-byte compressed key on a **256 KiB** worker stack.
Malformed, noncanonical, zero-valued, and value-free terminal images fail closed. The complete Bag
suite passes **22/22**, the isolated construction-allocation gate passes **1/1**, the affected
EPathMap matrix passes **183/183**, and strict lint passes for both production libraries. Randomized
`BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, u64>` and legacy `HashMultiSet` oracles distinguish the Bag's exact-key pointwise
lattice from PathMap's generic prefix-aware lattice; exact PathMap lookups and copy-on-write updates
preserve Bag laws without changing PathMap. Multiplicities 1 and `u64::MAX` allocate the same one
trie entry and have the same construction-allocation count; the largest ACTree03 scalar image is
only eight bytes larger because the branchless `u64` varint occupies one through nine bytes. Rocq
kernel-checks exact-key independence, the sum monoid, distributive lattice, subtraction, and
normalized/canonical delta laws. Verus with `--no-cheating` verifies the executable `u64`
underflow/overflow boundary and successful normalized reversal. The complete Rocq, Verus, Z3, TLC,
and mCRL2 bundle passes. This is constant-native-stack, semantic-equivalence, allocation-shape, and
formal evidence for the standalone Bag.

Checkpoint `cd01ea721` then makes the normalized delta the live datum-consumption commit carrier for
both play and replay. The accepted candidate vector is scanned iteratively; fresh and persistent
candidates are skipped, and each nonpersistent stored PathMap identity records one exact removal.
Repeated identities collapse into a multiplicity rather than an occurrence vector. `BagDelta`
clones the authoritative PathMap root once, mutates only changed trie frontiers, and publishes only
after every exact removal, checked addition, and RhoPath validation succeeds. The hot store holds one
write lock for that publication. No recursion, traversal cap, `RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, or
alternate stack is introduced. End-to-end comparative memory remains open.

Checkpoint `21ece399d` binds that live transition to three complementary formal models. Rocq proves
that only stored nonpersistent candidates contribute exact removals, permutation of the same
accepted candidates produces the same play/replay delta, and rejected publication exposes the
unchanged Bag. TLC exhaustively checks **3,942 generated / 2,628 distinct states** at depth 3 for
exact multiplicity, persistent/fresh exclusion, accepted-result equality, rejected-state
immutability, and whole-root publication. mCRL2 proves the implementation process
branching-bisimilar to its atomic reference contract and independently proves that observable
partial-key publication is unreachable. The full bounded proof script passes Rocq, Verus
`--no-cheating`, Z3, all three TLC models, and both mCRL2 obligations under **1 GiB per-tool caps and
zero swap**. This closes the abstract live-commit transition obligation; concrete generated-query
soundness and full RSpace schedule/post-state equivalence remain open consensus obligations.

Checkpoint `0f9beb5f0` removes the redundant enclosing `RSpaceDataStore` root clone without weakening
that publication model. The store validates every delta path before mutation, then `BagDelta` owns
the one private copy-on-write root and publishes it only after the complete normalized transition
succeeds. Late underflow, overflow, and malformed-path controls include an earlier valid operation
and still observe the complete pre-state. Pgmcp experiment 218 accepts the preregistered singleton
latency hypothesis: 245.370 ns control median versus 231.454 ns treatment median (**5.671% lower**),
82 raw samples per arm, Welch `p = 1.1743230270934331e-138`, and Cohen's `d = -15.668`. The four
secondary cardinalities improve by 0.950–3.008% rather than regressing. This microbenchmark closes
the duplicate-root cost it isolates; it is not an end-to-end RSpace allocation or RSS result.

Checkpoint `87679597d` next measures one moving PathMap write zipper across the sorted exact-key
operations of a `BagDelta`. The zipper moves through each successive longest common prefix rather
than replaying every path from the root; leaf deletion prunes value-free structure before the next
move. Experiment 219's preregistered 256-change primary has 51 samples per arm: median latency falls
from 22,924.652 ns to 22,650.136 ns (**1.197%**) and mean latency falls **1.929%**. Welch's
`p = 4.5845472558e-7`, Cohen's `d = -1.050`, Cliff's `delta = -0.472`, and Mann-Whitney
`p = 4.0848091004e-5` support the direction, but the primary effect does not clear the campaign's
separate five-percent end-to-end selection threshold. More importantly, the singleton treatment
regresses **8.289%** at the median because there is no adjacent prefix to reuse, while cardinalities
16 and 4,096 improve **10.058%** and **8.172%**.

Checkpoint `9a746f2bf` therefore makes the mechanism adaptive: an empty delta returns without a COW
fork, a singleton uses the lower-overhead direct exact-key mutation, and a multi-key delta uses the
moving zipper. All **23/23** Bag tests pass, including randomized legacy and `BTreeMap` oracles,
late-failure rollback, the deep/wide small-stack gates, and an exact-prefix case that deletes a leaf
between adjacent updates. The change alters physical traversal only: exact counts, publication,
failure atomicity, ordering, and byte images are unchanged. It is not an end-to-end memory result;
the enclosing scope was capped at 8 GiB with zero swap, but a post-exit RSS high-water mark was not
available and is not inferred.

At the initial SS-A11 checkpoint, the guarded-search workload retained its expected algorithmic counts: the 1,000-datum single-bind
exhaustive guard performed 1,000 spatial matches and 1,000 guard checks in 17.303 ms; the 60-by-60
guarded join performed 3,660 spatial matches and 3,600 guard checks in 11.653 ms; the unguarded store
needed two spatial matches in 1.878 ms. These are one-run regression observations, not comparative
throughput claims.

The first post-catalog control/treatment pair is also **not a throughput claim**. Another agent ran a
large unit-test workload concurrently; once discovered, the host load average was 58.62. Both arms
are invalidated and excluded from pgmcp measurements, report conclusions, and optimization verdicts.
The preregistered 51-sample, 99%-confidence comparison remained pending until the corrected
instrument and clean run described below.

The first retained-automaton attempts likewise established no timing verdict. Intermittent test load
continued after the implementation landed, so no result from those attempts was admitted.
Benchmark checkpoint `7bc5c6994` then corrected a more fundamental instrument defect: the original
matrix timed `consume` against resting data, a path that never consults the produce-side retained
automaton. The accepted control/treatment matrix instead installs persistent waiting receives and
times the completed COMM caused by `produce`; the control disables only the matcher's retained-path
hooks while treatment enables them. It selects the canonically last matching receive so control
executes its complete candidate scan. Under 51 samples, 99% confidence, CPU-8 affinity, 5 GiB RSS,
zero swap, and preflight load 5.38/32 with no competing Rust build/test process, all six confidence
intervals are disjoint. Treatment latency is **18.8–30.8% lower** and throughput is
**23.2–44.6% higher** for 16, 256, and 4,096 waiting receives under both diverse and shared prefixes.
Each treatment upper latency bound is below 95% of its control lower bound, satisfying the
preregistered five-percent threshold without relying only on point estimates. A Casper
test observed later began after the benchmark file's completion timestamp. The retained-automaton
throughput hypothesis therefore passes for this exact-ground slice; at that checkpoint direct
automaton/Bag products, construction cost, allocations, and the broader workload matrix remained
open. The recorded estimates
are [`measurements/rspace-retained-pathmap-prefilter-2026-08-15.tsv`](measurements/rspace-retained-pathmap-prefilter-2026-08-15.tsv).

The paired resting-datum control/PathMap benchmark at `564dac0b4` is admitted to the measurement
ledger. The run used 51 samples per arm at 99% confidence under a 5 GiB no-swap scope on the
32-physical-core host. Approximately six cores were occupied at preflight, below the user-approved
stop threshold of 30; scheduler affinity was unrestricted. Treatment throughput is **43.9–55.0%
higher** at 16 distinct entries, **12.39–13.30 times** control at 256, and **239–259 times** control
at 4,096. Every treatment interval at those sizes is disjoint from control. At one entry the result
reverses: treatment throughput is **7.1% lower** for diverse and **11.4% lower** for shared prefixes,
also with disjoint intervals. The crossover supports structural prefix pruning for nontrivial pools
but rejects a blanket “never regresses” claim; a single-entry bypass or lower-fixed-cost query must
be tested before final layout selection. The scope's 1.5 GiB peak includes compilation and therefore
does not establish allocation or steady-state RSS. Raw estimates are
[`measurements/rspace-resting-pathmap-prefix-2026-08-15.tsv`](measurements/rspace-resting-pathmap-prefix-2026-08-15.tsv).

That falsifying singleton result was repaired at `0b601ce67` by recognizing a structural base case:
a physical pool with at most one candidate has no proper subset for an index to select. The PDA
therefore takes its existing canonical direct scan before any retained-path construction, zipper
descent, position allocation, or sort. The focused test observes one spatial match and zero retained-
path queries. All **392** package tests pass. In the repeated eight-pair matrix, the diverse
singleton is 2.2% faster and the shared singleton has a statistically neutral +0.6% point estimate;
both arms execute the same direct-scan code, so these small differences are not attributed to the
treatment. Treatment retains **48.7–53.4%** higher throughput at 16, **12.22–13.01 times** control
at 256, and **238.8–256.9 times** control at 4,096. Raw post-repair estimates are
[`measurements/rspace-resting-pathmap-singleton-repair-2026-08-15.tsv`](measurements/rspace-resting-pathmap-singleton-repair-2026-08-15.tsv).

The standalone Bag microbenchmark at harness commit `7b3254573` is a separate admitted result. A
first run was interrupted and discarded as soon as another session began unit tests; its Criterion
result directories were deleted before the accepted run. The clean preflight found **74% aggregate
idle** on the 32-physical-core, SMT-disabled host. The release executable completed in **4 min
50.69 s** under **8 GiB `MemoryMax`**, zero swap, and unrestricted affinity; postflight idle was
82%, and peak process RSS was **39,912 KiB**. Each arm used 51 samples, 2 s warm-up, a requested 5 s
measurement interval, 99% confidence, and 1% significance.

Against legacy `HashMultiSet`, PathMap Bag construction latency is **20.5–54.6% lower** across 1,
16, 256, 4,096, and 16,384 distinct shared-prefix keys. Full exact-lookup-sweep latency is **3.5–37.8% lower**
at every size except 4,096, where it is **0.236% higher** with disjoint confidence intervals; this
is recorded as operationally neutral rather than a universal-win claim. Clone followed by one
update is **55.1% lower latency** at 16 keys and **98.1–99.975% lower** from 256 through 16,384
because PathMap shares structure, but at one key its fixed cost is **65.9% higher**. That falsifying
singleton point remains in the ledger. With one distinct key, construction latency stays approximately
**76 ns** while logical multiplicity grows from 1 to `u64::MAX`; this agrees with the isolated
allocator gate that occurrences are not expanded. The 39,912 KiB figure covers the complete
benchmark process and is not a comparative heap or per-operation RSS measurement. Raw estimates
and resource metadata are
[`measurements/pathmap-bag-microbench-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/pathmap-bag-microbench-2026-08-16.tsv).

The live publication experiment is separate from that standalone HashMultiSet comparison. It asks
whether `RSpaceDataStore` needs an outer COW clone around `BagDelta`'s already-private atomic root.
The 32-core, SMT-disabled host was 59–64% idle immediately before the one accepted run; the process
was pinned to CPUs 0–7 in one shared-L3 CCD with the performance governor. It completed in 53.53 s,
peaked at 570,124 KiB RSS under an 8 GiB cap, and used zero swap. Each arm and cardinality has 82
samples. The singleton median improves **5.671%** (245.370 ns to 231.454 ns), satisfying both the
five-percent effect threshold and the locked Welch/effect-size criterion. Cardinalities 16, 256,
4,096, and 16,384 improve **3.008%**, **0.977%**, **1.436%**, and **0.950%**. Raw measurements and
sealed pgmcp digests are
[`measurements/rspace-bag-single-root-commit-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/rspace-bag-single-root-commit-2026-08-16.tsv).

The follow-on cursor experiment isolates whether a delta with sorted shared-prefix keys should
restart each exact mutation at the root or preserve one moving PathMap write-zipper focus. The one
accepted run began with 74% aggregate idle CPU on the same 32-core, SMT-disabled host, no competing
Cargo or rustc process, and CPUs 0–7 pinned under an 8 GiB cap with zero swap. Each arm and
cardinality has 51 samples. The primary 256-change median improves **1.197%**, while the 16- and
4,096-change medians improve **10.058%** and **8.172%**; the singleton median regresses **8.289%**.
The selected implementation consequently uses direct mutation for zero/one operation and the
cursor for multi-key deltas. No peak RSS is claimed because the enclosing scope's post-exit
high-water mark was unavailable. Raw measurements, full statistics, and sealed pgmcp digests are
[`measurements/rspace-bag-delta-cursor-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/rspace-bag-delta-cursor-2026-08-16.tsv).

The next experiment asks a different question: whether the receive-first product should replace its
two mutable read zippers with two borrowed `TrieRef` handles and construct a descendant focus for
every accepted byte. Commit `514659e2b` contains both the frozen zipper control and the treatment;
both return the exact same sorted candidate vector before timing. The one valid run used 82 samples
per arm and cardinality, CPUs 0–7, the performance governor, an 8 GiB cap, and zero swap. Preflight
showed 87–88% aggregate idle CPU and no Cargo or rustc process. One Apalache process occupied roughly
two cores, far below the user-approved 30-core stop threshold.

The treatment is slower throughout. At the primary 256-candidate fixture, mean latency moves from
71,177.181 ns to 115,273.666 ns, a **61.953% regression**. The locked
treatment-less-than-control Welch test gives `t = 1355.572`, `p = 1`, and Cohen's
`d = +211.705` in the wrong direction; Cliff's `delta = +1` and the Mann-Whitney result agree.
Mean regressions at 16 and 4,096 candidates are **83.041%** and **55.549%**. PathMap's borrowed
`TrieRef` is appropriate for stable query-start views, but its descendant operation reconstructs
in-node focus-key state; doing that for each byte loses to a zipper that moves and ascends in place.
Checkpoint `27557c374` therefore retains paired mutable read zippers in production. Native-stack
complexity remains $`O(1)`$; this decision changes the explicit heap control representation, not the
PDA or its accepted candidates.

An earlier attempt was stopped when the user clarified that another coverage suite was merely
between tests. It completed neither arm of the paired primary endpoint and is excluded from every
verdict. Its active Criterion directory was quarantined before the valid run. The complete accepted
ledger and that exclusion are
[`measurements/rspace-query-product-trieref-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/rspace-query-product-trieref-2026-08-16.tsv).

##### 5.16.5.5 Datum-first retained-automaton × Bag product

The predecessor used its retained waiting-pattern trie only against the arriving datum. If the
channel already contained data, it disabled that prefilter because a legal communication may
consume a resting datum and leave the arrival stored. Checkpoint `ad395c357` replaces that bypass
with a product over the retained `PathMap<TerminalId>` and authoritative
`Bag(PathMap<Multiplicity>)`. Both zippers occupy the same escaped structure-prefix byte domain.
Their child-mask intersection drives an explicit depth-first heap stack, so only byte edges present
in both tries are visited. Reaching a retained terminal admits its continuation to the ordinary
candidate scan; residual wildcard/capture instructions and the spatial matcher still decide the
verdict. The product can therefore preserve a false positive but cannot create an acceptance or
hide a prefix witness if its trie traversal is sound.

This closes the resting-only schedule without constructing a unit-valued copy of the Bag, decoding
records, enumerating occurrences, or converting either trie to a vector. Bag multiplicity remains
one `u64` value at the complete record key and is irrelevant to the existence question. The fresh
datum follows the same retained segment through an allocation-free framed-byte iterator. Canonical
candidate order is unchanged because the result remains a bitmap over the predecessor vector.

The first two measurements are retained failures. Experiment 224's byte-at-a-time product won at
diverse/256 and both 4,096-candidate cells, but the long shared-prefix primary at 256 moved from
888.96 ns to 1,870.04 ns and was rejected. Experiment 225 used compressed unary descent and cut that
treatment to 1,054.76 ns, but its contemporaneous 920.97 ns control still won by 14.5%; it too was
rejected. These results isolate the fixed cost of walking a long common byte prefix when the
authoritative exact matcher is unusually cheap.

The singleton-Bag specialization uses `Bag::distinct_len`, which is a cached derived scalar, to
borrow the sole complete trie path once. Compilation records one local `usize` per distinct
terminal byte depth, sorts it, and removes duplicates. This vector is a generated traversal
schedule, not a candidate collection, serialized surface, or alternative EPathMap/Bag
representation. If no non-root terminal depth can prefix the Bag key, selection returns after the
root fallback. If exactly one can, one exact `PathMap::get` visits it. If more than one can, the
zipper resets and the linear product runs. The dispatch therefore avoids a repeated-prefix-search
sum in the many-depth case: exact probing is bounded to one lookup, and the fallback visits common
trie edges once.

Release preflight caught an implementation defect before experiment 226 collected a timing sample:
`to_next_val` and two `ascend_byte` state changes were initially called inside `debug_assert!`.
Optimized Rust removes the assertion expression, so release traversal remained at the wrong focus.
Checkpoint `61accc170` executes every zipper movement unconditionally and checks only the resulting
invariant in a debug assertion. The release regression covers both singleton and multi-depth
fallbacks, diverse/shared 16/256/4,096 candidates, embedded zero bytes, and branching Bags.

Experiment 226 accepted the repaired schedule at 932.83 ns control versus 216.08 ns treatment for
shared/256. The final complexity-bounded source was then preregistered and measured separately as
experiment 229. It records **840.48 ns versus 207.20 ns** at shared/256, a **4.06× speedup**, and
**13.712 µs versus 1.183 µs** at shared/4,096, an **11.59× speedup**. Its locked primary Welch test
gives $`t = -1040.8646`$, $`p = 1.6872 \times 10^{-171}`$, Cohen's $`d = -162.5557`$, and a 95%
mean-difference confidence interval of $`[-634.4884, -632.0678]\,\mathrm{ns}`$. Shared/16 remains
slower, **136.23 ns versus 52.70 ns**, and is recorded as a fixed-cost crossover rather than hidden behind a universal-win
claim. All arms contain 82 post-warm-up samples from one CPU-8-pinned run under an 8 GiB, zero-swap
scope; no Cargo or rustc process competed at preflight. The scope cap is not a comparative RSS
measurement. Raw summaries, rejected designs, statistics, and sealed pgmcp digests are
[`measurements/rspace-retained-bag-product-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/rspace-retained-bag-product-2026-08-16.tsv).

##### 5.16.5.6 Immutable revision lifecycle and residual-query representation

Checkpoint `4f63119c0` makes the retained automaton's lifecycle and eligibility observable. Each
compiled value is an immutable projection of one complete live continuation-group revision. A
version change constructs and publishes a replacement; it does not mutate the old value or append
tombstones. Therefore $`L = T`$ and $`D = 0`$, where $`L`$ is the live-terminal count, $`T`$ is
the terminal-arena length, and $`D`$ is the dead-terminal count. A proposed dead/live rebuild
threshold cannot improve this representation because its predicate is unreachable. The focused
regression rebuilds slices from 1 through 512 candidates and observes the invariant at every size.

Operational counters now expose total and indexed candidates, total/indexed/fallback patterns,
total and distinct terminal paths, shared terminals, compile count/time, and cache hits. These
counters permit captured-workload eligibility and terminal-sharing measurements without decoding
stored records or retaining a second collection. They do not alter the authoritative
`PathMap<TerminalId>`, its candidate order, or the `Bag(PathMap<Multiplicity>)` product.

Experiment 241 asked whether identical residual `RhoPathQuery` programs should be hash-consed into
an append-only arena addressed by fixed-width `QueryId` values. The local treatment used a transient
hash table with full equality on collisions; the control kept one owned query per terminal. Both
arms constructed the same transition chain and passed an exact-selection preflight. The one-shot
CPU-8 run collected 82 post-warm-up samples per arm and cardinality under an 8 GiB, zero-swap scope.
The arena regressed mean construction latency by **28.59%** at 16 candidates, **10.27%** at 256,
and **5.98%** at 4,096. At the preregistered 4,096-candidate primary, control was
**1,685,976.60 ns** and treatment was **1,786,732.56 ns**. The one-sided Welch test rejected the
predicted decrease ($`t = 173.2981`$, $`p = 1.0`$, Cohen's $`d = 27.0646`$; 95% mean-difference
interval $`[99,607.55, 101,904.37],\mathrm{ns}`$). Production consequently retains owned residual
queries; the rejected arena exists only inside the reproducibility benchmark.

The resulting production automaton compiles, selects, and drops a one-million-byte-deep terminal
and a 20,000-terminal-wide chain on a 128 KiB worker stack. A separate counting allocator confirms
that doubling 1,024 live terminals to 2,048 remains below threefold growth in both allocation count
and allocated bytes. The focused release gate passes **11/11** automaton cases plus **1/1** isolated
allocation case, and strict Clippy passes for the production library, both tests, and the benchmark.
The raw summaries, sealed pgmcp run digests, preregistration, and rejection are recorded in
[`measurements/rspace-retained-query-arena-2026-08-16.tsv`](measurements/rspace-retained-query-arena-2026-08-16.tsv).

##### 5.16.5.7 What it cost

Native-stack complexity changes from $`\Theta(b)`$ to $`O(1)`$. Explicit control storage is
$`O(b)`$, which is the irreducible selected-candidate/frame frontier. Search time and output storage
remain proportional to the candidate combinations actually visited and, for enumeration, emitted.
The machine creates one frame per live bind, one chosen-candidate entry per selected bind, and one
copy-on-write authority Bag plus one initially empty reservation Bag per distinct channel. A frame
records only an optional reservation position; it does not clone either trie. Reservation space is
linear in the number of distinct identities simultaneously demanded, bounded by the live bind
frontier, rather than channel cardinality. The derived catalog is linear in distinct records rather than total
multiplicity. Its path topology and lazy decode cells are shared across pool snapshots;
multiplicity-only changes update derived counts without rebuilding it. The traversal does not
materialize a Cartesian product or expand duplicate trie keys. The retained automaton adds one trie
terminal relation per bind position and a temporary selection bit vector linear in the number of
waiting continuations. Cache hits perform no trie clone. The exact-ground slice walks the arriving
datum path, so its native stack remains $`O(1)`$. The direct automaton/Bag product also uses constant
native stack. Its explicit depth-first level vector is $`O(d)`$ for maximum common trie depth $`d`$,
and it visits $`O(e)`$ common byte edges for a multi-key or multi-depth query. The singleton/single-
depth specialization performs $`O(\log s)`$ schedule partitioning plus at most one exact lookup,
where $`s`$ is the number of distinct terminal depths. It never repeats exact lookup for multiple
eligible depths.

For a supported receive-first pattern, the synchronized product scan allocates one heap vector
containing only the matching fixed-width catalog positions and sorts it in $`O(m \log m)`$, where
$`m`$ is the number of surviving candidates, before the final spatial checks. The full-scan control
is $`O(n)`$ in distinct channel records. Native-stack use remains $`O(1)`$ in both cases because the
zipper and query machine are iterative. Product traversal visits only byte edges present in both
tries and never materializes their Cartesian product. The admitted curve shows that the original
prefix collection/sort decisively wins once the pool has 16 entries in the tested worst-order
workloads. The proof-derived zero/one-candidate base case removes the known fixed-cost loss without
choosing an empirical cutoff. Ordered nested instructions now descend their first exact byte run
before enumerating a complete frame; their explicit closer and capture maps use heap space linear in
the live nested frontier and repeated-capture count, while native-stack use remains constant. The
associative-commutative schema instructions and allocation-per-COMM
remeasurement remain open measured questions rather than settled claims.

##### 5.16.5.8 What is still recursive

No candidate-selection or enabled-rendezvous recursion remains. The first production-only pgmcp run
after SS-A11 reported two direct findings and three mutual clusters across the wider target. Source
inspection established that both direct findings and two clusters were `#[cfg(test)]` recursive
oracles still physically under `src/`. They now live under `models/tests/support` or
`rholang/tests/support`, reached only through `#[cfg(test)]` path declarations; the production census
therefore falls from 28 to 25 dispositioned files while an exact-path gate independently scans the
26-member normalizer oracle and the git-provenance suite verifies 23 cited blocks plus six declared
mechanical deviations. Five of those deviations preserve destructive `locally_free` cache transfers
after `Par` gained custom iterative `Drop`: move the whole `Par`, `mem::take` the byte vector, then
move the emptied child into its parent. A clone-only E0509 adaptation was rejected by the differential
gate with **4 failures / 300 passes** because it retained a duplicate `[1]` cache in the nested
`Par` and changed canonical protobuf bytes; the transfer-preserving form restores **9/9** focused
normalizer differential cases and **8/8** provenance checks. The one genuine classic-pgmcp residual
is the reducer's eleven-function evaluator SCC.
This repair introduces no depth limit, stack-growing dependency, PathMap fork, or non-trie fallback
representation.

##### 5.16.5.9 Anti-vacuity

The 20,000-bind test enters both public modes on a 256 KiB thread: `consume` must return all 20,000
data candidates, while `enabled_rendezvous` must enumerate exactly one 20,000-candidate selection.
That pair fails if either former recursive body is restored, if the selector short-circuits before the
deep leaf, or if enumeration omits the continuation. Existing guarded tests separately reject cursor,
rollback, ordering, guard-veto, and metric drift. The source census must count both removed recursive
components; its 574-to-572 change supplies the structural anti-vacuity witness.

The multiplicity refinement adds two orthogonal anti-vacuity witnesses. One test requires two
identical nonpersistent occurrences to fill two binds without an expanded occurrence vector. Another
requires exhaustive enumeration to emit exactly one rendezvous for those indistinguishable
occurrences, then fires it and observes cardinality zero. Exact-path data-index tests independently
remove one of two identical occurrences and observe multiplicity one before the final removal.

The resting-prefix refinement adds four more witnesses. A worst-canonical-order corpus requires the
control to call the spatial matcher 256 times and the indexed scan exactly once. A key containing an
embedded zero rejects delimiter-based prefix shortcuts. A deliberate prefix false positive must
still be rejected by the spatial oracle. Finally, 64 generated corpora compare the full and indexed
selector result, RSpace event trace, and post-state maps, so a vacuous empty scan, reordered scan, or
unchecked derived membership fails observably.

The nested refinement adds independent framing and traversal witnesses. Its RMP1 corpus contains
zeros that differ after one and two escaping layers; using the in-memory matcher on a stored product
frame therefore fails the production differential. The selected nested target is canonically last,
so the control must make 256 spatial calls while the product makes one and returns the same result.
Every proper truncation of a shallow token stream is rejected, and the 20,000-level/128 KiB test
fails if native recursion or a fixed traversal cap is reintroduced.

The datum-first refinement uses the same canonically-last construction against 256 persistent
waiting receives. The control arm must visit all 256; the retained-query arm must visit one; both
must return the same COMM and leave byte-equivalent event and state projections. A residual exact
term after a wildcard separately forces the terminal query to run rather than treating its retained
prefix as a complete verdict. Root fallback and the 4,096-terminal chain prevent unsupported or
shared-root candidates from being pruned vacuously.

##### 5.16.5.10 Authoritative `ParBag` exact-membership crossover

Checkpoint `6fcbb520e` adds the typed foundation for the final `Par` authority: one versioned

#### 5.16.6 Sparse relational-row reuse inside the production PDA [SS-A10 refinement]

##### 5.16.6.1 The repeated-work defect

The stack-safe conversion had already removed native recursion, but the production
`spatial_matcher_pda::ListMachine` could still re-evaluate the same pattern/target edge whenever
an augmenting path displaced an earlier assignment. The compatibility `MaximumBipartiteMatch`
surface exhibits the same graph problem, but it is **not** the production driver; older task and
architecture prose that named it as production was stale. `sub_pars` remains upstream of the
list machine for connective remainder enumeration.

Let $`P`$ be the pattern-row count, $`T`$ the target count, and $`E`$ the number
of successful cacheable edges discovered. A dense table would require $`\Theta(PT)`$
retained cells even when the relation is sparse. Re-scanning would retain less memory but could
perform the same structural match many times. Neither choice is necessary.

##### 5.16.6.2 Sparse prefix-plus-delta relation

`f1r3node-rust-mettail@3a3db311` introduces one shared `LazyRelation` utility used by
both the production list PDA and the compatibility matcher. Every cacheable row stores:

1. one integer frontier delimiting the target prefix already evaluated; and
2. only its successful edges, in discovery order.

A resumed augmenting frame first consumes the successful edges that existed when the frame was
created and then evaluates only the unseen suffix. The cursor's snapshot bound prevents a frame from
immediately replaying an edge it just discovered. Failed edges need no bitmap: membership in the
evaluated prefix plus absence from the successful-edge vector is sufficient. Retained relation
storage is therefore $`O(P+E)`$, not $`O(PT)`$.

Remainder filler rows are deliberately non-cacheable because their cheap locally-free predicate is
dense and their result payloads would dominate the sparse relation. Concrete successful edges share
one empty binding delta. Structural edges retain only the binding **delta** produced relative to the
attempt baseline, not a clone of the complete `FreeMap`. Before final assignment
materialization, the relation releases its references so `Rc::try_unwrap` can move unique
deltas instead of cloning them.

This is an internal refinement of the existing PDA. PathMap-backed set and map carriers still enter
as `PathMap<()>` and `PathMap<Par>`; exact subtraction, owned/read zippers, canonical
byte keys, and the singleton paths described in §5.16.2 remain unchanged. No trie snapshot,
`Vec<Par>` projection, PathMap reconstruction, mixed-mode carrier, or PathMap crate
modification was added.

##### 5.16.6.3 Deterministic experiment

The preregistered D-E4 displacement graph has 128 pattern rows and 128 targets. Target zero has no
incoming edge, while every later row can displace the preceding assignment. Both arms execute from
the same production-shaped graph and binary. Because every exact-counter replicate is identical,
sample variance is zero; a Welch statistic is undefined. The frozen protocol therefore decides the
primary metric by exact inequality rather than inventing variance. **MEASURED:**

| control | samples | calls/sample | result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| nominal no-cache displacement schedule | 51 | 699,263 | rejecting assignment, as constructed |
| production sparse relation | 51 | 16,384 | same rejecting assignment; every pair evaluated at most once |
| exact difference | 51 paired constants | 682,879 fewer | **42.67962646484375× fewer calls** |
| diagonal invariant, both implementations | one exact control each | 8,256 | same successful assignment; zero cached-edge visits and zero row reuse |

The displacement treatment additionally asserts positive row reuse and cached-edge visits,
$`\mathrm{evaluated\_pairs} \leq |P||T|`$, and at most $`2|P|`$ successful edge
evaluations. The diagonal control prevents a nominally easy graph from appearing faster merely
because instrumentation or traversal order changed. The 51 control and 51 treatment constants,
digests, commands, and gate rows are committed in
[`measurements/relational-ac-edge-reuse-2026-08-10.tsv`](measurements/relational-ac-edge-reuse-2026-08-10.tsv);
the human-readable experiment record is
[`../../scientific-ledger/d-e4-lazy-relational-ac-edge-reuse-2026-08-09-2026-08-10.md`](../../scientific-ledger/d-e4-lazy-relational-ac-edge-reuse-2026-08-09-2026-08-10.md).

##### 5.16.6.5 PathMap connective-domain algebra and ownership closure

Commit `f1r3node-rust-mettail@4f022ad9b` removes the next repeated-work layer without
changing the spatial matcher that decides an edge. Before the checkpoint, a list element whose sole
carrier was `ConnOr` or `ConnAnd` compiled to the universal candidate domain. The sparse relation
therefore avoided re-evaluating an edge, but it still had to ask the authoritative matcher about
every previously unseen target. The new compiler builds a conservative domain expression:

```text
exact structural atom       -> Query(RhoPathQuery)
OR(p1, ..., pn)             -> Union(compile(p1), ..., compile(pn))
AND(p1, ..., pn)            -> Intersection(compile(p1), ..., compile(pn))
NOT(p), unsupported carrier -> All
empty OR                    -> Empty
empty AND                   -> All
```

`All` means “do not prune”; it never means “accept.” An unsupported arm of an OR therefore makes
the whole union `All`, while an unsupported arm of an AND contributes no restriction. Negation is
not compiled by complementing a conservative query, because the complement of a superset is an
unsound subset. The original spatial PDA still evaluates every surviving edge and remains the sole
verdict and binding authority.

The target index maps each generated structural prefix to fixed-width, big-endian `u64` positions.
Those eight-byte keys are prefix-free: no encoded position is a proper prefix of another. Native
`PathMap<()>` lattice operations therefore implement exact finite position-set algebra at this
boundary despite PathMap's generally prefix-aware lattice semantics. Union uses `join`, intersection
uses `meet`, and only the final algebraic result is materialized and sorted into predecessor target
order. Query lookup retains the existing prefix zipper visit. The intermediate tries retain
PathMap's persistent copy-on-write sharing; no `Vec<Par>`, hash-set reconstruction, trie snapshot,
or PathMap crate change is introduced.

The implementation is an explicit work machine rather than a recursive compiler. In literate
pseudocode, its invariant is that the value stack contains exactly one compiled plan for every
completed `Enter` task:

```text
work <- [Enter(root)]
values <- []
while work is not empty:
    task <- pop(work)
    if task is Enter(pure OR children):
        push(ReduceUnion(number of children))
        push each child as Enter in reverse source order
    else if task is Enter(pure AND children):
        push(ReduceIntersection(number of children))
        push each child as Enter in reverse source order
    else if task is Enter(other pattern):
        push(conservative atom query or All/Empty)
    else if task is ReduceUnion(n):
        push(join of the last n values)
    else if task is ReduceIntersection(n):
        push(meet of the last n values)
assert values contains exactly one plan
```

The first depth-20,000 diagnostic exposed a separate ownership defect before this algorithm could be
called resource-safe. An OR continuation retained `Arc<[Par]>` and cloned the selected child, so a
singleton chain copied every recursive suffix. The 8 GiB, zero-swap systemd scope was OOM-killed
after **43.746 s** with an **8 GiB peak**. Replacing indexed clones with owning iterators removed the
heap explosion, but the next run was still interrupted after **98.768 s** at **208.1 MiB peak**:
each pure-connective `Par` recomputed cardinality bounds over its complete remaining suffix, giving
$`\Theta(d^2)`$ work at nesting depth $`d`$.

The final checkpoint moves connective plans, candidate/remainder pairs, and AND/OR children through
owning iterator frames. The final AND or OR branch consumes the remaining target owner instead of
cloning it. Cardinality analysis gains a borrowed entry, and a `Par` containing exactly one
connective with no remainder transitions directly to that connective. This transition is equivalent
to the general subset machine: every proper-subset candidate leaves a nonempty complement, which
must fail against the empty residual pattern, so only the whole target can succeed. Compound-target
positive and proper-subset negative cases compare both verdict and `FreeMap` with the independent
recursive oracle.

After both root causes were removed, one test builds, matches, and destroys a depth-20,000 singleton
OR chain and a depth-20,000 singleton AND chain on a **256 KiB** native thread stack in **0.18 s**.
The complete focused equivalence module passes **15/15**. Its width-128 rejecting connective chain
records **699,263** nominal edge visits and **254** production visits in each of 51 exact-counter
replicates, while the successful diagonal remains **128** production edges. Strict production-library
Clippy passes with warnings denied. The broader all-test lint reaches 107 pre-existing warnings in
unrelated normalizer and pretty-printer tests; no warning names an affected source.

The counters establish causal work reduction and non-vacuity. Commit `efc48ab0d` then isolates the
domain algebra in a default-disabled differential benchmark: the control forces the former `All`
domain, while the treatment uses the production `PathMap<()>` join/meet plan. Both arms retain the
same ownership, iterator, direct-transition, and stack-safety repairs, so the benchmark does not
confound the algebra with those common changes. Fixture construction and cloning occur outside the
timed interval.

#### 5.16.7 Byte-native exact-key EPathMap algebra inside the production PDA

##### 5.16.7.1 The projection defect

The general associative-commutative `PathMachine` was already an explicit heap-backed PDA, but its
exact EPathMap preparation discarded the representation advantage it had been given. Each exact set
or map key was decoded to `Par`; a second EPathMap was constructed as a typed mask; subtraction then
encoded those keys again to reach the target's trie. The implementation therefore paid decode,
allocation, and re-encoding cost for an equality fact already present in canonical bytes.

This defect did not consume depth-proportional native stack. It was nevertheless on the same hot
matcher path and retained allocation proportional to exact-key count. A larger stack, `stacker`, or
an artificial traversal limit could not repair it.

##### 5.16.7.2 Selected representation boundary

`f1r3node-rust-mettail@92240a452` makes exact-key matching byte-native. Allocation-free canonical
metadata distinguishes an exact key from one that requires semantic matching. Exact set and map keys
enter one mode-independent `PathMap<()>` mask. `EntryTrie::subtract_encoded_keys` and
`select_encoded_keys` apply that mask directly to the target's existing trie; map values remain
stored as `Par` payloads and are borrowed only when their value pattern is evaluated.

A dynamic key is different: Rholang matching can bind variables or evaluate connectives, which raw
equality cannot answer. It is decoded exactly once during pattern preparation and retained across
search. A concrete map key with a dynamic value compares raw key bytes and runs the spatial matcher
only on the value. A free remainder selects surviving raw entries, while a wildcard remainder
materializes nothing. This boundary is therefore semantic rather than cardinality-tuned:

```text
exact key       canonical bytes -> PathMap mask/algebra
dynamic key     canonical bytes -> one Par decode -> spatial semantics
stored map value PathMap<Par>    -> borrow existing Par -> spatial semantics
```

`f1r3node-rust-mettail@03685f4c7` then gives map subtraction one copy-on-write root and one moving
write zipper across lexicographically ordered encoded keys. Deletion uses `remove_val(false)` and
`prune_ascend`; selection advances paired read/write zippers and never clones a source value merely
to decide membership. Set subtraction already delegates the equivalent unit-valued PathMap
operation. Neither checkpoint modifies PathMap, EPM1, protobuf, bincode, or the homogeneous
`Empty | Set(PathMap<()>) | Map(PathMap<Par>)` model.

Pgmcp experiment 233 measures 16, 256, and 4,096 exact entries plus one wildcard remainder, which
forces the production general `PathMachine`. Criterion used 82 post-warm-up samples, 99% confidence,
one-percent significance, a two-second warm-up, and a five-second requested measurement interval.
The executable was pinned to CPU 8 on the 32-physical-core, simultaneous-multithreading-disabled AMD

Cargo or rustc process competed at preflight.
