### 5.41 Descriptor-complete codec and byte-native admission equivalence [SS-E5]

#### 5.41.1 The evidence defect

The schema generator already emitted a protobuf decoder entry point for every ordinary `rhoapi`
message, but the executable differential selected only five non-`Par` roots. A new descriptor
message, field, or oneof arm could therefore compile into the generated pushdown automaton without
entering an independent recursive-oracle gate. This was an **evidence defect**, not a newly found
recursive production traversal: the generated decoder and admission machines were already
explicit-worklist implementations.

#### 5.41.2 Architecture and rationale

`models/codegen/schema.rs` now emits a seventh artifact, compiled only by unit tests. It is derived
from the same resolved descriptor rows as the six production artifacts and contains no second
message inventory. For each of the 56 generated messages it builds canonical witnesses for the
default value, each field, repeated cardinalities one and two, every oneof arm with default-valued
presence and a nondefault scalar witness, numeric boundaries, and the all-fields-populated shape.

Each witness follows this executable differential:

```text
descriptor witness bytes
  ├─ generated protobuf PDA ── generated re-encoder ──┐
  └─ untouched Prost oracle ── Prost re-encoder ──────┼─ exact byte equality
                                                     └─ strict byte admission
decoded generated value
  ├─ generated bincode PDA ───────────────────────────┐
  └─ derived serde/bincode oracle ────────────────────┴─ exact byte equality
```

`Par` and `EPathMap` remain the only explicit extern adapters. Their fixtures construct the
authoritative `ParBag`, neutral `EPathMap`, `PathMap<()>` set mode, and `PathMap<Par>` map mode
directly. No fixture calls `trie_snapshot()` as a traversal surrogate, projects a trie to
`Vec<Par>`, sorts decoded entries, or rebuilds PathMap from a flattened representation.

Descriptor-known wrapper messages with no RPB3 scoring role use an opaque semantic summary after
their complete recursive wire structure has been validated. Unknown or mismatched programs still
fail closed; the generated registry is the closed authority that permits the opaque case.

#### 5.41.3 Results and anti-vacuity

The focused module passes 21 of 21 tests. Its generated arithmetic is 56 ordinary messages plus 2
externs, 5 oneofs with 54 arms, 329 canonical witnesses, and 48 ordinary scalar fields whose
explicit default presence must be rejected. Every canonical witness is byte-identical across both
protobuf implementations and both bincode implementations. Successful admission reports exactly
one byte-native validation and zero typed decodes, reconstructed-key bytes, and endpoint replays.

For every generated fixture in all nine RPB3 families, a test-only arena cursor returns the exact
byte-native score and compares it with the score/body split already resident in the authoritative
RPB3 key. Completeness, family, and canonical-path stability agree as well. Raw-`Par` controls prove
that multiplicity changes the score, root `locally_free` does not, and `connective_used` does. ESet
and EMap controls pin first equality-representative retention and greatest-value collision
selection. The score observation and its `Vec<u8>` are absent from non-test builds.

The hostile matrix applies every truncation, duplicate complete image, unknown field, and
nonminimal first key to all 329 fixtures. Ordinary messages use decode-plus-exact-reencode;
component roots additionally require the independent authoritative RPB3 body fixed point. Targeted
mutations cover tag zero, wrong wire types, boolean aliases, duplicate singular/oneof fields,
groups, invalid UTF-8, nonminimal/oversized lengths, every EPM1 fixed framing layer, ACT corruption,
value-count mismatch, homogeneous-mode confusion, trailing bytes, and mixed legacy/current fields.
Five test-only state mutants independently set reconstructed-key, endpoint-replay, typed-decode,
skipped-validation, and repeated-validation counters; an omitted-multiplicity score is a sixth
executable red observation.

The former depth-4,096 admission fixture was replaced by an iterative byte builder for a
20,000-level `Par` / `Expr::ENot` spine. It and a 4,096-element wide `ParBag` complete on 256 KiB
native stacks. The builder performs one bottom-up length pass and one root-down write pass; it does
not retain every recursive AST suffix.

#### 5.41.4 Resource and residual statement

Wall-clock microbenchmark, allocator profile, and retained-heap deltas are **NOT MEASURED — SS-E5
is a correctness/anti-vacuity instrument and changes no selected production algorithm**. The
captured debug module run completes 21 tests in 0.36 s after compilation, and the full `models`
library passes 279 of 279 in 4.71 s. The respective SHA-256 log digests are
`4624c47b83cc964a7bca732abbd066f4bb7221c8969f42133b5968d9376c6c87` and
`ca7545c2a3c6e96fc1853d818fcfb5f47689b3f46dc521ce26b2c2d69cd0a1c1`. These are test-runner

At the SS-E5 checkpoint, the single-parse ACT plan, production RPB3 cutover, full RSpace lifecycle

### 5.42 Single-admission ACT plan and EPM1 consumer closure [SS-C15]

#### 5.42.1 Mechanism and boundary

An ACT (`ACTree03`) image is PathMap's physical prefix-compressed trie representation. Before
`bdaf93a5f`, the newer indexed topology route admitted that image into `ValidatedActPlan`, while
Bag import and several EPathMap routes still used the older metadata-map parser. Direct EPM1 decode
also inspected the ACT arena and then parsed it again during live `PathMap` reconstruction. Both
implementations were iterative, so this was not a native-stack regression; it was redundant linear
work and proportional metadata retained across adjacent stages.

The selected boundary is now:

```text
untrusted ACT bytes
  -> one stack-safe physical admission DFS
  -> immutable preorder ValidatedActPlan
       |-> endpoint cursor -> Bag / EPathMap reconstruction
       |-> value summary   -> Set/Map ordinal admission
       `-> topology cursor -> byte-native EPM1/RPB3 reducers
```

Admission proves canonical varints, offsets, producer order, sparse/dense branch order, line
placement/reuse, exact line-hash collision equality, complete arena coverage, and root/trailer
closure before a logical event becomes observable. The plan retains source offsets for values,
edges, and line bytes. The contiguous and indexed/fragmented cursors therefore share the same
accepted language and event order while the indexed cursor maps a logical offset back to exact
physical provenance.

At this historical checkpoint, ordinal facts were folded during the same physical DFS: set mode
required zero markers and no external value table; map mode required sequential preorder ordinals
and agreement with the EPM1 value count. The later positional V6 association supersedes that map
rule: every EPM1 ACT value marker is zero and map bodies associate in logical value-bearing
endpoint order, independently of allocation addresses. Value-free endpoints consume no body.
Marker/count admission still precedes observable topology. J-155 and the
ACTree03 invariant catalog retain the successor authority; the old ordinal scheme is not the
current format.

Task 5981's September 17 reconciliation confirms that the single-admission successor preserves
explicit value-free childless endpoints while rejecting redundant unary branches and empty line
wrappers. This is an admission-language correction, not a traversal optimization or a new measured
stack/heap reduction. [J-008](../pathmap/pathmap-engineering-journal-2026-08-23.md#j-008--2026-08-23-admit-canonical-explicit-value-free-endpoints)
records the fixing commit and executable witnesses; CBR-044 records the compatibility consequence.

#### 5.42.2 Space and traversal result

For physical ACT length $`a`$, semantic records $`S`$, folded line wrappers $`W`$, emitted logical
edge bytes $`e`$, maximum current endpoint length $`K`$, and branch depth $`D`$, validation plus one
walk has the derived bounds

```math
T(a,S,W,e)=\Theta(a+e),\qquad
H(S,W,K,D)=O(S+W+K+D),\qquad
N=O(1),
```

where $`H`$ is transient heap and $`N`$ is native-stack space. Instrumented construction requires
exactly $`S`$ semantic-node parses and $`W`$ wrapper parses. `node_reparses` and
`event_metadata_source_reads` are hard-zero sentinels; only compressed line bytes are reread when
their logical `Edge` events are emitted. `rewind` resets indices and explicit stacks without
revalidating the source.

A complete one-line endpoint lends its exact input range. A key that crosses a branch edge uses one
reusable path buffer; retained EPathMap inspection owns only those branched keys. Bag and EPathMap
reconstruction insert directly from the cursor into `PathMap<Multiplicity>`, `PathMap<()>`, or
`PathMap<Par>`. No route projects the trie to `Vec<Par>`, sorts entries, or creates a hash-based
semantic shadow.

Generated pausable EPM1 value decoding keeps one current borrowed protobuf-body range. It compares
the generated PDA result with that body immediately, stores only the first failure ordinal, admits
and reconstructs ACT once, and reports a delayed body error afterward. The delay preserves the
pre-existing ACT-before-body error precedence without retaining $`O(n)`$ body ranges. Publication
still occurs only after the complete snapshot succeeds.

#### 5.42.3 Executable evidence and limits

All commands ran in systemd user scopes with `MemoryHigh=6G`, `MemoryMax=10G`, and
`MemorySwapMax=0`:

| Gate | Result | Captured-log SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| focused EPathMap/ACT module | 24/24 | `be02a3ef2c44eecbc85b231c98238506a85089fa9c50f91f879eb487388a1d37` |
| validated-plan module | 12/12 | `56dc6a4df2acb630dd58e2e420077c1fa19c38741001e4959b640d8b3589c685` |

The matrix covers all ACT truncations and single-bit mutations against an independent parser,
aliases/gaps/overlap, sparse and dense branches, forced line-hash collision behavior, contiguous

This closes the measured metadata-replay mechanism and production-consumer migration. It is **not**

The earlier executable matrix established malformed rejection, differential topology, and bounded

All six proof-lineage and mutation-control files compile under a 1.5 GiB hard RSS cap with zero

not an artificial runtime traversal limit. Rust further replaces reverse-preorder identifier lookup
with one forward-preorder record per node and fuses finish-order replay into admission; executable
record-index and writer differentials bind those efficiency refinements.

The focused post-extraction gates pass 10/10 validated-plan tests, 17/17 formal-manifest tests, and
16/16 EPM1 writer-image tests. The first includes 128 arbitrary writer cases per property run; the

The complete integrated formal harness also passes across Rocq, Verus, Z3, TLC, and mCRL2. Its

### 5.43 Chunked history-leaf hashing [SS-C16]

#### 5.43.1 Mechanism

RSpace cold-history DATA, continuation, and join leaves each wrap one already-encoded `Vec<u8>`.
The frozen bincode-1 representation of that wrapper is an eight-byte little-endian length followed
by the resident payload. Before `583f21e44`, checkpoint preparation materialized that complete
wrapper into a second `Vec<u8>` solely to pass one contiguous slice to BLAKE2b-256.

The new `Blake2b256Hash::new_from_chunks` feeds the length and resident payload to the same
incremental BLAKE2b-256 state. Hash functions consume a byte stream, so chunk boundaries are not
semantic. The production helper nevertheless relies on no informal assumption: its exact output is
differential-tested against `bincode::serialize` for `DataLeaf`, `ContinuationsLeaf`, and
`JoinsLeaf`. Omitting the length prefix is an executed negative control and changes the hash.

#### 5.43.2 Resource result and limit

For payload length $`n`$, the retired route retained the original $`n`$ payload and allocated an
additional $`n+8`$ wrapper before hashing. The selected route retains the original payload and an
eight-byte stack prefix, then performs two hasher updates. Both routes are $`\Theta(n)`$ time and
$`O(1)`$ native stack; the selected route removes the proportional secondary heap buffer. The
complete `rspace_plus_plus` library passes 76/76 under `MemoryHigh=6G`, `MemoryMax=10G`, and
`MemorySwapMax=0`; the captured-log SHA-256 is
`f0130e46758de9f9c4122e8dcece395a732dacb1533f3d35ed90b8cf73797a2d`. The strengthened
all-wrapper 2/2 differential log is
`92bca75c8d51714fc53b8afc1d886a8354f1ae16265f3ed5f483fbe9eca7c7f7`.

This is a construction-level allocation result, not an allocator-profile or throughput result.
The legacy key-value boundary still owns a serialized `PersistedData` value. The later
PathMap-native persistence design remains differential and transactional through its WAL; it owns
object durability, commit records, catalog publication, recovery, compaction, and acknowledgement.
SS-C16 changes none of those stages and does not claim that the WAL is implemented.

### 5.44 Final persisted-value egress and borrowed admission [SS-C17]

#### 5.44.1 Mechanism and complexity

J-023's PathMap-native DATA egress previously stopped at the leaf payload. The repository then
serialized `PersistedData::Data`, allocating and copying that payload into the final cold-store
value. Derived deserialization copied it back out on reads and import verification. Checkpoint
`3061b2501` moves the frozen four-byte enum tag and eight-byte field length into the checked egress
plan. The plan reserves the exact final size once, writes the envelope, and expands each resident
identity according to `Multiplicity(u64)` without a typed or occurrence-vector intermediate.

`PersistedDataView` is a non-recursive checked cursor over that envelope. It lends the exact
single-field range used by the history hash and the payload range used by decoders. Its private
bincode-compatible parser retains trailing-byte behavior only for differential tests; every
authoritative storage reader/importer calls canonical admission and rejects a suffix not covered by
the declared leaf-hash range. Typed paths reuse their owned payload allocation and shift it once to
prepend the envelope.
All paths are $`\Theta(n)`$ in emitted bytes and $`O(1)`$ in native stack. The transient descriptor
arena remains $`\Theta(d)`$ for $`d`$ distinct identities because the frozen complete-identity order
can differ from structural PathMap order; J-024 rejected a duplicate persistent identity trie.

#### 5.44.2 Measured result

The v2 final-value matrix uses seven preregistered cardinality/multiplicity/prefix-sharing cells and
31 paired AB/BA observations per cell. Exact final length and BLAKE2b-256 leaf digest agree before
timing. Across 100,000 pair-preserving bootstrap resamples, every 99% treatment/control median-ratio
upper bound is below 0.385. Observed median ratios are 0.0323–0.3745. Exact allocation counters show
24–36,878 fewer calls and 2,668–4,583,789 fewer allocated bytes per operation.

| raw v2 matrix | `080db0fc751268ba41b9065edb449300e5de34fab23ef712640fc38b60825ad2` |
| statistical analysis | `b27a62e753b07a67164dbb6fa8bdc383b936f608f95ed4a9c85a9588ca8a3e56` |

#### 5.44.3 Limits and anti-vacuity

Exact all-variant envelope differentials cover payload lengths 0, 1, 255, and 65,537. Admission is
compared with derived bincode over every truncation, every header-bit flip, trailing bytes, and a
hostile maximum length. The compatibility oracle accepts bincode's trailing suffix while
authoritative canonical admission rejects it. Canonical and typed checkpoints produce identical
roots; property tests preserve multiplicity; export/import passes through the shared cursor. The
benchmark asserts final bytes and digest equality before every timing sample, so a faster wrong
format cannot enter the statistics.

Verus proves the complete envelope-length boundary in addition to occurrence/cardinality
arithmetic. TLC's good model requires validation, private header construction, complete payload
construction, and one atomic publication. Required failing mutants expose partial publication,
missing framing, and skipped validation; executable Rust mutants expose omitted multiplicity and
the wrong identity-order domain. The proof therefore cannot pass merely because it omits one of
the final value's observable layers.

This is a heap/allocation refinement, not a new recursion conversion. It does not implement the
future PathMap-DAG object store or its WAL. That design remains differential and transactional and
retains separate object sync, commit-record sync, catalog publication, recovery, compaction, and
acknowledgement obligations.

### 5.45 Certified ParBag protobuf egress and atomic replay [SS-C18]

#### 5.45.1 Mechanism and stack boundary

The generated protobuf machine was already stack-safe, but an outer RSpace frame could visit the
same copy-on-write `ParBag` owner once for every `Par` shell that referenced it. The former adaptive
path therefore performed $`r`$ authoritative PathMap traversals for reuse count $`r`$. A global
cache would have introduced lifetime, invalidation, retained-memory, and concurrency obligations
that do not belong at a serializer boundary. Caching every frame-local owner would also tax the
common singleton case.

SS-C18 performs one exact preflight census over the generated outer schema. Component-empty `Par`
values remain direct because they have no PathMap component body. Singleton owners remain direct.
For a repeated owner, the first occurrence emits the canonical component body from the
`PathMap<Multiplicity>` zipper and records ranges in the private output; later occurrences replay
those ranges and emit their own root metadata. One reusable owner stays inline. A hash table is
allocated only when a second reusable owner is first recorded. Correctness is independent of the
optional statistics observer.

The same preflight builds a typed pre-order transcript. It reserves each `MessageBody`, `ParBody`,
`MapEntryBody`, or `EPathMapSnapshotBody` event before descending and completes it after the child
succeeds. Sixteen event kinds and lengths plus a `u16` completion set are inline; larger schedules
spill to one vector. Emission must replay the exact type and length sequence, exhaust every recorded
owner range, and produce the planned body length. The frame is private until all checks pass, so a
failure cannot publish a prefix. EPathMap snapshot bodies continue to use the homogeneous
`PathMap<()>` or `PathMap<Par>` representation directly; there is no element-list projection or
sorting step.

All control paths use $`O(1)`$ native stack. Transcript space is $`\Theta(e)`$ for $`e`$ generated
schema events, output is $`\Theta(n)`$ for $`n`$ published bytes, and owner bookkeeping is
$`\Theta(o_r)`$ for the number $`o_r`$ of distinct repeated owners. PathMap component traversal
work changes from $`\Theta(\sum_i r_i b_i)`$ to $`\Theta(\sum_i b_i)`$, where $`b_i`$ is owner
$`i`$'s component-body size and $`r_i`$ its occurrence count.

#### 5.45.2 Powered timing and physical attribution

The locked width-16/body-256 matrix uses 20 warmups and 101 balanced AB/BA retained pairs per reuse
cell. Every sample checks byte equality, output length, allocation counters, and PathMap traversal
counts before admission. The analysis uses 100,000 pair-preserving bootstrap resamples.

| Reuse | Treatment/control paired median | 99% interval | PathMap traversals, control $`\rightarrow`$ treatment |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 2 | 0.556835 | [0.551625, 0.567432] | 2 $`\rightarrow`$ 1 |
| 4 | 0.300896 | [0.298716, 0.305263] | 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 1 |
| 8 | 0.175201 | [0.173288, 0.179316] | 8 $`\rightarrow`$ 1 |
| 16 | 0.174705 | [0.171765, 0.177020] | 16 $`\rightarrow`$ 1 |

Headless Heaptrack uses a profile-only loop: fixture construction and warmup finish before

makes 99,235 calls and 65,353 temporaries, while the treatment makes 8,455 and 4,153 over 1,000

The complete command, provenance, hashes, raw observations, statistics, allocation results, and
counter table live in
[`measurements/parbag-certified-protobuf-egress-2026-08-26.md`](measurements/parbag-certified-protobuf-egress-2026-08-26.md).

#### 5.45.3 Equivalence and anti-vacuity

Executable differentials cover empty, singleton, skewed, and dense owner shapes; all production

`bc1ecbf6f0c2954a9a183cfbb530d2ea17bffd1ff86d19dbafa65a3c8cab6f3f`.

This checkpoint is a heap/time refinement inside the existing generated PDA, not a new recursion

### 5.46 Authenticated RSpace egress and affine import lifecycle [SS-C19]

#### 5.46.1 Mechanism and authority boundary

The former transfer interface exposed separate history, DATA, and root setters and inferred a
continuation from the final returned trie node. That divided one logical state-transfer transaction
into independently callable mutations: a caller could stage only part of a graph, appoint a root
before closure verification, or silently interpret an import error as stream completion. A
digest-only physical cold key also allowed distinct record kinds with equal payload digests to name
the same storage address.

SS-C19 makes pagination explicit and authenticated. Each page carries its traversal proof, exact
typed leaf projection, advertised next cursor, and terminal flag. Admission authenticates the page
and verifies its leaf count before decoding record bodies or mutating a store. Cold objects use a
domain-separated physical address over version, record kind, and logical digest; history edges and
roots continue to carry the unchanged logical digest. Empty state is one authenticated zero-object
terminal page rather than a special sentinel inferred from an empty vector.

One affine import session owns all staging authority. `seal` consumes an open session only after an
iterative verifier has proved the complete reachable closure. `publish` consumes the sealed session
and atomically publishes its verified-root set through a versioned root catalog. An `Activate`
session may advance current-root authority only if its captured generation still wins the catalog
comparison; a `PreserveCurrent` session cannot move that authority. Aborting either state consumes
the capability without publication. The process FFI preserves those ownership states with distinct
opaque open and sealed handles and exports no independent mutator compatibility shim.

Tuple-space bootstrap owns one `Activate(root)` session. Horizon synchronization owns one
`PreserveCurrent` session spanning all missing roots. Request states accept only the exact live
cursor; they stage before retiring it and use only the authenticated staging receipt to schedule the
successor. Stale, duplicate, or unsolicited pages perform no store mutation and create no new
request. Seal, publish, transport, and importer failures remain errors in the returned stream, and
initialization requires its terminal publication receipt before entering `Running`.

#### 5.46.2 Stack, heap, and concurrency bounds

Exporter traversal, page authentication, staging, and closure verification are explicit-loop
machines and consume $`O(1)`$ native stack with respect to trie depth. No operation introduces
`RUST_MIN_STACK`, `stacker`, a recursive fallback, or an artificial traversal-depth limit. The
closure verifier uses a fixed 1,024-entry/8 MiB CLOCK cache for decoded nodes and a fixed
4,096-address CLOCK cache for already verified cold leaves. It therefore avoids the former
input-sized leaf visited set while preserving bounded reuse for shared leaves. The remaining heap
frontier is the unresolved graph worklist required by the traversal, not a native-stack slope or a
second flattened state representation.

Horizon synchronization admits at most 32 live network requests and refills that window as cursors
complete. Timeouts resend only those bounded outstanding requests. Tuple transfer retains one live
cursor independent of page count; a 64-page regression holds active request-state cardinality at
one. Both drivers retain only authenticated cursor/session state, not `Vec<Par>` projections of
PathMap contents.

These are derived and executable resource bounds, not comparative timing or persistence-throughput
claims. The future binary WAL and content-addressed PathMap/ACT object store require separate crash,
recovery, compaction, and LMDB-control measurements.

#### 5.46.3 Verification and anti-vacuity

Resource-capped focused results are 17/17 state/authentication cases, 5/5 verified-root catalog
cases, 6/6 export/import cases, 12/12 tuple requester effects, 19/19 horizon requester effects, and
5/5 FFI lifecycle/error/unwind cases. The Casper test targets type-check with the fallible streams,
and symbol inspection finds exactly the six affine import operations while proving the four former
mutator symbols absent.

The TLA+ lifecycle control explores 148 generated states, 68 distinct states, and depth 10. Its
invariants require publication to consume a complete seal, at most one racing activation to publish,
and preserve-current import never to move current-root authority. Three independent required
mutants respectively publish an incomplete session, admit a stale activation, or let
preserve-current mutate authority; each fails its named invariant. The formal manifest requires the
control and all negative controls, so success cannot be obtained by removing publication, racing
activation, or preservation behavior from the model.

This checkpoint changes no canonical Rholang byte, logical cold-leaf hash, history root, COMM order,
matching verdict, post-state root, or metering rule. It does change the peer transfer schema:
requests carry an explicit cursor-protocol epoch and responses echo it with an authenticated
terminal claim. Those protobuf fields are additive, but an absent epoch is `UNSPECIFIED` and is
rejected; mixed old/new deployment therefore requires an explicit rollout bridge rather than
inference from an empty cursor. Explicit V1 alone uses the legacy empty terminal. V2 requires the
terminal cursor to equal the requested start cursor, and either protocol must agree with the
importer-authenticated staging receipt before state advances. CBR-053 records this state-byte-neutral,
corrective, network-rollout-visible boundary. It does not claim the planned persistent
PathMap-DAG/WAL backend or close CBR-053's independent continuation/join verdict and post-state axes.

#### 5.46.4 Atomic local checkpoints and typed legacy-state adoption

A **state authority** is the sole component permitted to mutate the history-object, typed
cold-leaf, verified-root, and current-root namespaces. Local checkpoints now enter that authority
as a `PreparedHistoryCheckpoint` bound to the exact base pair `(root, generation)`. One successful
memory lock or LMDB write transaction validates immutable-object collisions and the complete typed
closure, writes every new object, records verified membership, and advances the current root.
Failure, including a stale same-root ABA plan, leaves all four namespaces byte-for-byte unchanged;
a no-op advances neither bytes nor generation. Raw `rspace-*` and `eval-*` store-manager views are
read-only, and authorized `History::process` cannot bypass the transaction by committing a detached
radix root.

Legacy split stores and the older `rspace/casper/v2` layout use two phases. Structural staging
walks retained radix closures iteratively, verifies every content digest and canonical typed-leaf
envelope, copies immutable objects in batches of 256, and writes a versioned **pending manifest**.
That manifest binds the namespace, normalized retained-root set, selected current root, and closure
fingerprint. Split and v2 sources are accepted together only when they are exact mirrors. No root
membership or current-root authority is published during staging. When concrete RSpace types are
known, the generated datum, continuation, and join decoders validate every framed record through a
single transaction-bound closure verifier; that same transaction publishes the catalog, writes the
completed receipt, and removes the pending and raw legacy catalog keys. A completed receipt permits
legacy source files to be removed and does not pin the live current root after later checkpoints.
Receipts for `rspace` and `eval` are not interchangeable.

Both paths remain stack-safe. Radix traversal uses explicit worklists, and every logical history
path is constrained by the existing 33-byte RSpace key schema rather than an artificial traversal
cap. Closure verification retains the fixed CLOCK caches from §5.46.2. Migration's visited key is
the pair `(content hash, logical prefix)`, never the hash alone, because a shared immutable node may
appear at different typed logical paths. Phase-A orphan objects after a crash are harmless
content-addressed data; verified membership, current-root authority, and the completed receipt are
visible together or not at all.

Resource-capped executable evidence includes 13/13 local checkpoint authority cases, the 10/10
typed legacy-migration matrix for split, v2, namespace binding, interrupted/resumed staging,
removed and changed retained sources, strict manifests, malformed catalogs/history, and malformed
record refusal, plus the transaction-bound verifier suite. The
`RSpaceAtomicCheckpointAuthority` TLA+ control explores 357 generated states, 127 distinct states,
and depth 7. Three required mutants independently expose split object publication, root-only ABA
comparison, and trust in a caller-supplied target without a complete closure; each violates its
named invariant. These results establish atomicity, authority, stack, and recovery-boundary
properties. They are not an implementation or throughput claim for the later binary WAL and
persistent PathMap/ACT object store.

The post-integration executable gate passes the complete `rspace_plus_plus` library suite
**150/150** and its consolidated integration target **164/164** under zero-swap systemd scopes.
The release regressions that previously exposed incomplete campaign verification now also pass:
the corrected scratch-directory staging control **1/1**, `MakeMintTest.rho` **1/1** with all seven
registered cases completing, and `PoSTest.rho` **1/1** with all eleven registered cases completing.
The last result is an anti-vacuity completion observation, not merely a prefix of successful
assertions: each RhoSpec emitted its terminal `testSuiteCompleted` signal.

### 5.47 Continuation/join PathMap authority and rejected retained order indexes [SS-C20]

SS-C20 concerns two different orders over the same resident continuation or join group. The
**canonical order** is the bytewise order of complete frozen record bodies and is used for cold-
store serialization. The **operational order** is the historical newest-first scheduler order.
Canonical record bytes already form endpoint suffixes in the authoritative prefix-compressed
`PathMap`, so a read zipper produces canonical order without decoding a record, projecting
`Vec<Par>`, or sorting elements. Operational order cannot be inferred from trie order and remains
explicit fixed-width `u64` metadata.

The production operational projection walks the primary trie, collects borrowed `Arc` records with
their scalar ordinals, and sorts only those descriptors. Pgmcp item 6079 tested whether retaining an
additional ordinal-keyed PathMap would repay that sort. The 14-case matrix covers continuation,
resting-join, and installed-join shapes; 1--4,096 distinct records; join multiplicities through
4,096; shared and unshared prefixes; nine lifecycle operations; four projection-reuse levels; and
31 retained counterbalanced sets per cell. All arms preserve complete visible values, canonical
bytes and digest, primary/identity paths, multiplicities, ordinals, and length accounting.

Both candidates are rejected. The shared record/order trie has retained-byte ratios 1.035--11.048
and fails the 5% retained guardrail in 117 of 126 lifecycle cells. The payload-split candidate has
ratios 1.845--11.052 and fails all 126. Projection medians can improve to 0.268 of control, but a
single distinct join with multiplicity 4,096 makes deletion more than 304 times as expensive: the
candidate occurrence-expands one Bag endpoint into 4,096 retained order endpoints. This is the
wrong asymptotic representation even when repeated reads win. Production therefore retains its
single membership authority and transient scalar/borrowed sort.

The experiment is a heap/work and representation decision, not a native-stack conversion. Every
arm traverses with PathMap zippers and has $`O(1)`$ native-stack use in trie depth. It introduces no
depth cap, recursive fallback, enlarged stack, `stacker` integration, or PathMap source change. The
complete protocol, preregistered universal 5% guardrails, 100,000-replicate paired bootstrap,
Benjamini--Hochberg correction, allocation counters, raw matrix, and hashes are in
[`measurements/rspace-record-order-index-experiment-2026-08-26.md`](measurements/rspace-record-order-index-experiment-2026-08-26.md).

This result closes the retained-order representation choice. Canonical continuation/join egress now
preflights an immutable CoW root into a reusable plan containing the exact header, cardinality, and
encoded length, then replays borrowed zipper ranges into a fallible private sink. Empty collections
publish a delete without allocating a body. The current LMDB-compatible cold-store action is one
sink and therefore materializes one exactly reserved `Vec<u8>` immediately before that legacy
boundary; hashing, WAL, and page writers can consume the same plan without such a buffer. Replay
performs no `Vec<Par>` projection, record decoding, or element sort, and a sink failure cannot be
published.

The complete legacy-versus-PathMap lifecycle differential now runs a production PathMap store beside
an independent `HashMap`/`Vec` oracle over one deliberately non-vacuous fixture. The fixture preserves
the first representative of a source-free continuation identity, retains duplicate join
occurrences, and chooses two records whose digest-first scheduler order opposes their canonical
cold-store byte order. It then compares typed initial and final history roots, authenticated history
and cold-leaf closures, reset state, two distinct play COMMs, exact replay selection, final post-state,
and final export/import state. Nine named mutations change the observation: last-wins identity,
collapsed join multiplicity, reversed scheduler order, omitted COMM, lost reset join, lost checkpoint
occurrence, incomplete export closure, wrong replay selection, and retained removed continuation.

The resource-capped consolidated integration target passes **165/165** in **105.62 s** with log
SHA-256 `ff7843d7d89305fd8c8e9c0116279afa1cbd22575891256ee4d679f5d726d5ca`.
The composite proof runner closes the six axiom-free RSpace-commit Rocq capstones, verifies the
canonical-egress and continuation/join laws in Verus without cheating, obtains the expected Z3
`unsat`, accepts the TLA+ controls, rejects every named mutant with its required invariant witness,
and completes the mCRL2 checks. Its log ends in the five-tool success sentinel and has SHA-256
`6424ceb403d6af09c3648af5b38c00bc74ecc96c7668bb48ce0605a27eabe7c3`.
The full method and non-vacuity account are preserved in
[`measurements/rspace-continuation-join-lifecycle-equivalence-2026-08-26.md`](measurements/rspace-continuation-join-lifecycle-equivalence-2026-08-26.md).

This closes SS-C20's lifecycle and post-state equivalence obligation. The binary-WAL/
content-addressed PathMap-DAG persistence backend remains a separate implementation and throughput
obligation; none of the lifecycle evidence claims that it exists yet.

### 5.48 Canonical PathMap-DAG structural and semantic admission PDAs [SS-C21]

#### 5.48.1 Two proofs, because graph closure is not RSpace meaning

The first persistence-format milestone separates two properties that the older history verifier
could not safely conflate. A **structural closure** proves that every content-addressed object exists,
hashes to its reference, has the declared length and canonical adaptive radix shape, uses the
endpoint type assigned to its namespace, and does not form a cycle. **Semantic admission** proves
that each logical trie endpoint is a complete frozen RSpace key/value relation and that the three
roots agree across continuations and joins. A structurally canonical arbitrary byte path is not
RSpace state.

Both validators are explicit-worklist pushdown automata (PDAs). Structural traversal memoizes a
digest only for the expectation already proved, and compares a repeated digest's declared length
before taking that fast path. Semantic traversal deliberately does *not* memoize a DAG node by
digest: one immutable node may be shared beneath different logical prefixes, and each resulting key
must be checked. It carries one reusable byte path and work items of the form
`(object reference, parent path length, optional edge)`. Sibling scheduling comes directly from the
borrowed adaptive-node iterator; no child vector is constructed.

#### 5.48.2 Native-stack and heap bounds

For object count $`n`$, maximum logical key length $`k`$, and explicit frontier width $`f`$, native
stack use is $`O(1)`$ in object and key depth. Required heap space is $`O(n + k + f)`$ for structural
digest state, the semantic key buffer, and explicit worklists. Cross-root coherence performs exact
JoinBag lookup in $`O(k)`$ byte descent and uses PathMap set membership to quotient repeated channel
identities. Adaptive branch lookup is bounded binary search for Node4/Node16, direct slot-table
addressing for Node48, and bitmap rank for Node256.

Admission exposes total-resource ceilings for distinct objects, canonical bytes, references,
worklist entries, logical nodes, endpoints, logical path bytes, continuation-source bytes, join
lookups, and join-lookup steps. These limits bound hostile-input work; none is a recursion or
traversal-depth cap. Worklists use fallible reservation before fanout is appended. The continuation
RhoPath parser scans channel frames twice through a borrowed exact-size iterator rather than
allocating a retained frame-index vector. Recursive datum, pattern, continuation, and channel bodies
reuse the generated stack-safe cold decoders.

#### 5.48.3 Executable evidence and current limit

The focused resource-capped persistence module passes **29/29** cases. Its anti-vacuity matrix
includes a 20,000-object closure on a 256 KiB native stack; every adaptive child-class boundary;
direct lookup in all branch encodings; digest, length, collision, missing-object, endpoint,
branch, compression, and malformed-payload refusal; valid exact three-root state; exact frozen
decode/re-encode; channel/datum structure agreement; continuation pattern/channel arity;
preservation of an independently selected first-wins source; missing cross-root join refusal;
indexed-channel membership; repeated-channel quotienting; and independent structural and semantic
budget failures. The affected crate also type-checks under a 6 GiB RSS ceiling, zero swap, and four
compiler cores.

These are correctness and resource-shape results, not a persistence performance result. The module
is not connected to checkpoint publication, recovery, or current-root authority, so no LMDB/ACT
latency, allocation, retained-byte, disk-footprint, recovery-time, or compaction claim is made. The
next stack/resource obligation begins when the normalized mutation WAL streams these canonical
objects into durable packs. PathMap journal J-034 records the representation decision; CBR-053
records that the format remains dormant and consensus-neutral at this checkpoint.

### 5.49 Normalized PathMap mutation-journal cursor [SS-C22]

The next persistence component represents each touched semantic endpoint by its exact before and
after state. Data and joins use zero-or-positive `u64` counts; continuations use optional immutable
content references. A PathMap per namespace coalesces sequential changes, checks that the next
observed state equals the prior result, retains the original base state, and removes inverse
transitions that return to that base. This compare-and-swap form is the smallest replay language
that rejects a stale base and lets the later authenticated manifest/WAL layer recognize a wholly
installed target without applying an arithmetic delta twice. The base-to-target DAG compiler
itself accepts only exact `before` states; it never recognizes a target by mixing endpoint states.

Canonical preflight and emission retain immutable CoW roots and traverse them with read zippers.
For $`m`$ changed endpoints and $`b`$ total changed-key bytes, both passes take $`O(m+b)`$ time.
The retained mutation authority is the prefix-compressed trie itself, so no $`O(m)`$ entry
projection or sort is introduced. Decoder heap space is $`O(m+b)`$ for the admitted mutation tries;
native-stack use is $`O(1)`$ in key depth. Total entry and key-byte limits bound hostile input but
do not limit an individual path's depth.

Recovery can retain a validated borrowed view and iterate key ranges from the payload itself; it
does not need the producer-side PathMaps or an intermediate entry collection. Any producer error
poisons the complete builder, preventing publication of an earlier accumulated prefix.

The executable gate passes **14/14** focused mutation cases and **43/43** complete persistence
cases. Its depth anti-vacuity witness round-trips a 100,000-byte RhoPathV1 datum key on a 256 KiB
native stack. Malformed tests cover generation discontinuity, section permutation, duplicate or
descending keys, invalid RhoPath syntax, equal states, reference/presence corruption, trailing
bytes, and independent entry/key resource ceilings. A fixed digest pins the independently versioned
payload, a fallible sink proves direct replay stops on destination failure, and zero-copy pointer
provenance proves borrowed keys remain within the admitted input image. The production-library
Clippy gate also passes under the same dormant-module allowances used by SS-C21.

At SS-C22, this result proved the in-memory normalization and canonical streaming payload only.
SS-C23 now covers the affected-frontier DAG rewrite's bottom-up frame machine and private staging
overlay. Physical WAL scanning, pack recovery, catalog publication, and pack compaction remain
unimplemented and make no performance or crash-consistency claim here. PathMap journal J-035 gives
the byte/transaction rationale; consensus register CBR-053 retains the dormant classification.

### 5.50 Iterative affected-frontier radix-DAG rewrite [SS-C23]

The persistent compiler consumes the validated borrowed SS-C22 mutation view without rebuilding
its producer-side PathMaps. It authenticates the batch's exact base manifest and derives the
DataBag, ContinuationMap, and JoinBag roots from that sole authority. Its API requires a private
staging overlay rather than the generic immutable-store trait, so a failed later namespace or
resource check cannot publish a prefix of a transaction into the durable base.

For each ordered section, an adjacent-key cursor retains edit nodes only through the longest common
prefix. Referenced children are opened on demand; untouched subtrees remain content-addressed CoW
references. Prefix splits and deletion merges modify a flat edit arena. Finalization uses explicit
`Enter(node)` and `Exit(node)` frames: children complete before their parent, empty nonroots vanish,
endpoint-free unary nodes merge, and only nodes reachable from the finalized root enter staging.
No production call in this path is recursive.

The CAS driver compiles one exact immutable base: `actual = before` performs the mutation, while
`actual = after` and every third state reject the complete batch. Recompiling from that same base
is deterministic. Whole-transaction idempotence belongs to a later authenticated catalog
base/target comparison, never mixed endpoint acceptance. Explicit budgets bound total mutations,
loaded nodes/bytes, edited nodes, retained prefix bytes (including unary-merge edges), emitted
nodes/bytes, cursor nodes, and finalization frames. Store reads are length-bounded before
materialization, and unary merges preflight retained and emitted bytes before allocation. These are
hostile-input work limits and impose no trie-depth or Rholang-term-depth cap. Edited-node exhaustion
is also preflighted before suffix copies, split-fragment allocations, or referenced-child reads.

The focused rewrite matrix passes **22/22**, the staging-overlay matrix passes **4/4**, and the
complete persistence module passes **69/69**. Fixed differentials cover every compressed-prefix
relation, cascading deletion compression, the 4/5, 16/17, 48/49, and 255/256 adaptive boundaries,
all three typed roots, exact CAS, after/divergent-state refusal, deterministic same-base
recompilation, manifest authority, private later-namespace failure, cumulative resource refusal,
bounded physical reads, unary-allocation preflight, edited-node refusal before copying or reading,
staged reachability, and untouched-subtree nonloading. A 100,000-byte key tests unbounded
compressed-prefix handling. The anti-vacuity depth gate constructs 20,000
endpoint-bearing canonical nodes, changes the deepest endpoint on a 256 KiB native stack, and
matches a separately rebuilt target root. The resource-capped transcript SHA-256 is
`3ff9bf0e32d95723c837c32c93c59e48162a6893474e1e0c03bb57ffeec4e776`.

SS-C23 proves native-stack flatness and canonical CoW rewrite equivalence only. It does not prove
physical WAL scanning, durable object promotion, target-manifest validation, sync ordering,
catalog CAS, crash recovery, pack compaction, or LMDB migration/performance. Those operations must
receive their own explicit-worklist and failure-injection evidence before production activation.

### 5.51 Profile-typed differential transaction sealing [SS-C24]

SS-C23 deliberately stopped before a private rewrite could become publication authority. SS-C24
closes that in-memory gap without activating persistence. A **semantic profile** is a sealed Rust
type that binds one manifest to the exact channel, pattern, datum, continuation, and key-body
codecs whose invariants were verified. A **sealed transaction** is an immutable, portable delta:
it owns every newly required canonical object, borrows the exact admitted mutation bytes, and
carries the exact base version, target version, mutation digest, and profile identifier. It still
has no authority to update a durable catalog.

**Algorithm 37 (PROFILE-TYPED-TRANSACTION-SEAL).** The phase-typed PDA consumes each proof token
exactly once and exposes only the sealed result to the later durability layer.

```pseudocode
fully admit (base manifest, semantic profile) -> VerifiedDagState
require mutation.base = verified.version       -> Open
admit only referenced continuation-source blobs -> ContentReady
rewrite the affected frontier privately         -> Rewritten
encode and stage the profile-bound target manifest -> Manifested
verify incremental structural closure and RSpace meaning -> Validated
sort and own the reachable staged objects        -> Sealed
```

No method can skip a phase or manufacture its proof token. The target manifest embeds the
16-byte semantic-profile identifier, and both full admission and incremental admission reject a
different profile before typed interpretation. Staging retains caller-supplied logical bytes even
when an ambient store already contains equal bytes; consequently the sealed delta is portable to a
recovering process that has only the declared base. No production callback executes while the
staging lock is held.

Incremental closure may avoid reopening an untouched base subtree only with an inherited-boundary
certificate containing the semantic namespace, boundary kind, exact absolute byte path, and full
digest-plus-length reference. Digest equality alone is insufficient because one Merkle object may
occur at multiple logical paths with different RSpace meaning. Exact paths use interned,
segmentation-independent 64-byte chunks, so siblings share prefixes without retaining one complete
path buffer apiece. Failed extension rolls back every newly interned chunk and leaves the caller's
path unchanged. The rewrite and closure phases share one arena and one effective cap; the
simultaneously retained eligible and inherited boundary sets share one union cap. All new
provenance, closure, and full-admission digest-state hash-table growth is fallible. Full admission
checks its distinct-object and advertised canonical-byte ceilings before loading a new digest.
Staging object/byte ceilings and
changed-endpoint, logical-visit, exact-path, and provenance ceilings are aggregate transaction
budgets, not traversal-depth limits.

The incremental semantic PDA validates only changed DataBag, ContinuationMap, and JoinBag
endpoints. It computes the exact required JoinBag probes for changed continuations, detects vacated
join groups, and verifies the target values through direct adaptive-trie descent. It neither scans
the complete state nor projects trie entries into a vector. For affected frontier size $`f`$,
changed-key bytes $`b`$, and newly emitted bytes $`e`$, sealing performs expected/amortized
$`O(f+b+e)`$ rewrite and validation work, apart from codec cost for the changed values.
Native-stack use is $`O(1)`$ in trie and Rholang-term depth.

The independent canonical-rebuild oracle was itself converted to an explicit post-order work
machine, so the stack gate does not hide recursion in its expected-value generator. It handles a
100,000-byte path on a 256 KiB stack. A separately instrumented single-update matrix reads **2**
base objects at cardinality 1 and **5** at cardinality 256, then enforces an upper bound of **8**
through cardinality 4,096. This is affected-frontier evidence rather than a latency benchmark: the
extra reads describe radix depth, not a whole-state scan.

The resource-capped persistence module passes **96/96** cases in **1.81 s**. The transcript is
`target/scratch/persistence-transaction-sealing-final.log`, SHA-256
`4719f11ac0f0b6bfc6f682f9056fac166d755409ed6f53b1a62c9ced70330e54`. The matrix covers exact
base/profile authority, portable ambient-equal sources, missing and unreachable source refusal,
semantic rollback, deterministic object sets, aggregate staging and path budgets, path-location
and segmentation counterexamples, shared staged objects at distinct logical paths, 256 long
siblings, failure-atomic path interning, a cross-namespace provenance-union-cap mutant,
20,000-level closure/rewrite, a 100,000-byte complete seal, and a zero-object preflight mutant that
allows exactly one manifest/profile authority read and no structural object load. The run used a
6 GiB memory ceiling and zero swap; the target was already built.

SS-C24 still makes no physical durability, crash consistency, throughput, allocation, disk-space,
recovery-time, or compaction claim. Binary WAL framing and checksums, fsync ordering, catalog CAS,
restart recovery, pack publication, retained-root compaction/garbage collection, LMDB migration,
REPL integration, and comparative measurements remain separate implementation and verification
obligations. Merkleization supplies immutable object identity and sharing; later compaction traces
those references from retained roots and reclaims obsolete physical records. The two operations are
not synonyms.

### 5.52 Single-copy transactional log-pack codecs [SS-C25]

SS-C25 converts the sealed transaction's first physical traversal into a streaming, cursor-driven
codec before filesystem publication is activated. A fixed prepare header is preflighted from the
profile-typed receipt, borrowed normalized mutation bytes, and digest-ordered sealed objects. The
publisher first performs one digest-ordered committed-object pass. Missing objects become DATA;
equal objects become address-free REUSE only after complete length-and-byte comparison; unequal
same-digest objects refuse the plan before the first write. The fallibly allocated plan retains one
disposition per sealed object and no body copy. The writer then emits the header, checked-u64
CRC32C, mutation slice, and each disposition/reference plus only DATA bodies directly to a fallible
non-seeking sink. It retains only fixed hash/checksum state and counters; it cannot return a prepare
identity after any sink error. New object bytes are therefore written once rather than buffered or
copied into a separate WAL representation, while a warm store does not rewrite equal bodies.
The release writer also compares its counted output with the preflighted length before emitting the
terminal CRC; disagreement returns a typed invariant error and no identity.

The decoder validates the fixed header checksum before trusting variable lengths, checks the whole
record checksum, applies checked `u64` total-resource ceilings, parses the mutation as a borrowed
view, and walks object records with one cursor. Canonical object framing, digest, declared length,
and strict digest order are revalidated. A later iterator yields the already validated borrowed
ranges. It does not rebuild producer PathMaps, recurse through keys, project entries, or sort them.
The separately fixed **384-byte** commit record binds the store identifier, nonzero sequence, prior
commit digest, exact prepare address and digest, sealed base/target/profile/mutation receipt, and
durable index frontier. It also authenticates first-live pack, index generation,
retention-manifest reference, current-state canonical bytes, and retained-union canonical bytes so
the later catalog cannot mutate them independently.

The record view proves physical and canonical framing only. It is not a verified durable state:
same-digest collision equality against the object store, target-manifest closure, and semantic
profile admission remain mandatory recovery phases before catalog authority may advance.

For $`m`$ mutation bytes, $`o`$ logical canonical-object bytes, $`i`$ inline bytes, and $`n`$
object records, classification/preflight is $`O(m+o+n)`$ time with $`O(n)`$ one-disposition space;
streaming is $`O(m+i+n)`$ time with $`O(1)`$ additional writer state. The borrowed decoder adds
$`O(1)`$ state outside the canonical payload parsers. All are $`O(1)`$ in
native stack with respect to RhoPath, trie, and transaction depth. Total record, mutation, object,
entry, and key-byte limits bound hostile work without imposing a traversal-depth limit.

The focused matrix passes **14/14**. It checks every
prepare and commit truncation; independent authenticated-header and payload corruption; resource
refusal before payload parsing; exact prepare/commit round trips; fixed commit size; valid-record
negative rebinding of store, sequence, address length, prepare digest, and receipt; prior-commit and
address digest sensitivity; unrelated-receipt and invalid-extent construction refusal; borrowed
object order; exact agreement between the prepared layout iterator and parsed object offsets; a
destination failure that cannot produce a prepare identity; cold DATA versus warm
REUSE; collision refusal before writer construction; and nonzero checksum high-bit refusal. A
frozen V1 fixture pins the exact prepare header, 1,123-byte cold-prepare length/checksum/digest, and
complete 384-byte commit image. A transition containing a 100,000-byte identity seals, streams,
and validates on a 256 KiB native stack. The independent CRC test pins Castagnoli/iSCSI CRC32C of
`123456789` to `0xe3069283`. Captured transcript:
`target/scratch/wal-codec-packid-final-2026-08-27.log`.

This is a codec/resource class result, not yet a crash-durability result. No file is opened and no
data-sync, commit-sync, catalog-slot, directory-sync, recovery, index rebuild, compaction, garbage
collection, LMDB cutover, or performance comparison is claimed. J-038 in the PathMap engineering
journal records why the WAL and object pack share one physical stream. The next obligation is an
affine durable-I/O phase machine with injected failure at every write and synchronization boundary.

### 5.53 Retained-root manifest and exact catalog authority [SS-C26]

SS-C26 represents retained state without a recursive collection or a production-side vector. A
canonical retention manifest names one current `StateVersionV1` and a strictly ordered sequence of
historical versions, each paired with its checked canonical-closure byte inventory. The borrowed
view verifies domain, version, count, order, current exclusion, exact consumption, and lower byte
bounds once; `RetainedStateIter` then advances one fixed record at a time. Its native stack and
cursor state are constant in history length.

Two fixed 336-byte catalog slots appoint dormant physical authority. Selection validates checked-
`u64` CRC32C, all reserved bytes, store/profile agreement, equal-or-adjacent epochs, exact 384-byte
commit address, live-pack range, commit-end-equals-durable-tail, nonzero/aligned index generation
and tail, retention reference, and logical/retained byte inventories. An observably incomplete
inactive prefix preserves the prior slot. Once the low CRC32C half is present, the remaining four
high bytes already have their required zero value in an empty slot; such a prefix is byte-identical
to the completed successor and is correctly accepted.

Recovery additionally binds a selected slot to the commit loaded at its exact address. Store ID,
sequence, commit digest, target state, semantic profile, and the full publication tuple must all be
equal. The commit-side publication constructor enforces the same `64 + 72n` index frontier as the
catalog, eliminating a transient state in which an unaligned authenticated commit could parse but
only fail later at catalog construction.

This separation is required for restored storage metering. Current-state canonical closure bytes
are deterministic logical input. Retention policy, WAL/index/catalog framing, dead tails, and old
pack generations are physical metrics. The implementation records both, but physical local-policy
overhead cannot change consensus charges.

Catalog tests pass **6/6**; retention tests pass **4/4**. They cover every retention truncation,
frozen zero-history bytes, strict-order and current-duplicate refusal, adjacent selection, every
observable inactive-slot tear, incompatible slots, corrupt-only images, exact CAS/epoch overflow,

### 5.54 Portable log-pack and rebuildable object-index layouts [SS-C27]

SS-C27 closes the physical-layout ambiguity between SS-C25's transaction records and SS-C26's
catalog frontier. `PackId` is a nonzero `u64`; zero is reserved solely for the genesis predecessor
sentinel. Genesis is pack 1 at sequence 1. A successor advances pack identifier and first sequence
consecutively and authenticates the prior pack identifier plus terminal-commit BLAKE2b-256 digest.
The exact **128-byte** header has fixed domain/version/width, store and chain identity, flags,
reserved-zero bytes, and zero-extended CRC32C. The parser rejects all truncations, counter overflow,
nonconsecutive links, identity substitutions, unsupported flags, reserved bytes, and checksum-width
mutants without recursion or input-sized allocation.

Each rebuildable object-index generation begins with an exact **64-byte** store/generation header.
One **72-byte** record binds `ObjectRefV1` to a nonzero pack, canonical-body offset, and transaction
sequence. A borrowed file view admits only the exact catalog-appointed `64 + 72n` prefix and ignores
the physical suffix; records remain lazily fallible so corruption requests rebuild rather than
changing semantic state. Pack and index widths are centralized in the durable layout module and are
the same constants enforced by terminal-commit and catalog construction.

The WAL preflight is the sole object-offset calculator. Its exact-size layout iterator walks the
already digest-ordered sealed objects and DATA/REUSE disposition slice together, carrying the
record-relative body offset. The index append plan verifies store identity, pack-header exclusion,
complete prepare extent, aligned old tail, and checked new-tail arithmetic. It converts DATA
layouts directly to absolute index locations and skips REUSE. Thus the index path performs no
second record parse, canonical-body copy, `Vec<Par>` projection, semantic sort, or duplicate offset
arithmetic.

For $`n`$ sealed objects and $`d`$ DATA objects, layout traversal is $`\Theta(n)`$ time with
$`O(1)`$ iterator state; index emission is $`\Theta(d)`$ time with $`O(1)`$ writer state. Native
stack is $`O(1)`$ in object count, trie depth, and key length. The persistent sealed transaction
still owns the $`O(n)`$ disposition plan required for pre-write collision classification.

The pack suite passes **5/5**, and the 2026-08-27 post-freeze hardening extends the affected
persistence matrix to **134/134**.
Frozen little-endian images pin all 128, 64, and 72 bytes. Negative matrices cover every
truncation, corrupted and valid-checksum-mutated fields, nonzero/counter/link invariants,
catalog-tail alignment and suffix exclusion, store mismatch, prepare-offset/extent overflow, index
tail overflow, DATA/REUSE location derivation, and canonical-object extent overflow. The aggregate
persistence gate passes **134/134** in **1.67 s** under 4 GiB, zero swap, and an eight-core quota.
Captured transcripts are `target/scratch/pack-codec-v1-final-2026-08-27.log`,
`target/scratch/wal-codec-packid-final-2026-08-27.log`, and
`target/scratch/persistence-durable-layout-final-2026-08-27.log`. The post-freeze transcript is

Storage accounting deliberately separates logical inventory from physical telemetry. The

### 5.55 Affine durable startup and single-PathMap index repair [SS-C28]

SS-C28 implements the first filesystem-backed restart boundary without promoting it to semantic
RSpace authority. On Unix, `DurableDirectoryV1` pins an owner-controlled directory descriptor and
opens generated one-component names relative to it with no-follow behavior. A process-wide affine
writer lease owns the pinned directory and advisory lock. Regular-file, single-link, owner,
owner-only-mode, exact-length, short-I/O, and checked-offset invariants fail closed. The threat
boundary assumes processes sharing the same user identity cooperate with the lock; an equally
privileged noncooperating process already has authority to rewrite the store and is outside this
lease protocol.

The first iterative pack scan constructs the only
`PathMap<ObjectIndexRecordV1>` and compares any existing exact-length physical index record by
record. Repairable shape or checksum damage never becomes semantic-state loss. SS-C30 subsequently
refined repair to pre-admit twice the exact catalog-appointed pack span, stream the second pass
directly into a fixed candidate, synchronize its exact length, atomically replace the generation,
synchronize the pinned directory, and verify the installed file directly against the first-pass
PathMap. The second pass uses a constant-state sink that requires every DATA record to equal the
first-pass PathMap location and every REUSE to resolve strictly backward; direct index verification
allocates neither another trie nor a record vector.

The authority sequence is:

```text
exact catalog image
  -> bounded WAL scan + one PathMap + optional index probe
  -> exact catalog comparison
  -> [verify existing] or [stream candidate -> sync file -> replace -> sync directory]
  -> parse installed index and verify directly against first PathMap
  -> exact catalog comparison
  -> IndexBoundPhysicalRecoveryV1
```

The writer object owns the lease while the physical snapshot is observable. Raw mutation consumes
that snapshot first, so no caller can retain an old catalog token beside unrestricted writable
handles. A later mandatory typestate must load objects through the bound index, prove the current
semantic closure, derive exact current and retained-union byte inventories, and validate the
retention manifest before production code may treat the root as semantic RSpace authority.

For catalog-appointed WAL bytes $`S`$ and distinct DATA records $`d`$, verified startup performs one
$`\Theta(S+d)`$ pass. Following SS-C30, repair performs $`\Theta(2S+2d)`$ physical work but retains
one $`O(d)`$ PathMap and $`O(1)`$ replay state. Native stack remains $`O(1)`$ in pack count, record count, key
depth, and term depth. `DurableStartupWorkV1` reports WAL passes and bytes, index bytes read and
written, and synchronization counts; these are restart-work diagnostics, not persisted footprint
or consensus charges.

The Unix I/O suite passes **11/11**; the startup/failpoint suite passes **7/7**; and the complete
dormant persistence matrix passes **153/153** in **1.69 s** under a 5 GiB high/6 GiB hard memory
cap, zero swap, and an eight-core quota. Failure injection covers candidate write, exact truncate,
file sync, pre-replace, post-replace/pre-directory-sync, directory sync, catalog changes at each
verification phase, and post-install index damage. The construction counter proves repair creates
one committed PathMap total. Logs are
`target/scratch/durable-io-after-startup-2026-08-27.log`,
`target/scratch/durable-startup-failpoints-2026-08-27.log`, and
`target/scratch/persistence-durable-startup-checkpoint-2026-08-27.log`.

This remains a dormant Unix physical-recovery result. Windows native handle/ACL operations,
semantic and retention-inventory admission, bounded generation compaction, reader-safe garbage
collection, LMDB migration, REPL activation, and comparative latency/allocation/disk evidence remain
unclaimed. The active I/D/T consensus tariff is unchanged; closure-size inventories are only
deterministic metadata until separately admitted and versioned.

SS-C29 completes the dormant generation-checkpoint publication protocol from a verified abstract

Formal verification preceded implementation. The formal obligations were extracted into 74 stable

traceability property requires exact equality among the catalog, derivation matrix, and Rust
binding registry; resolves every TLA+ and Rocq symbol; requires every base invariant and capstone to
be cited; and proves every witness configuration is part of the integrated gate. The production
refinement began only after that check was green. The resource property was deliberately observed
red first: semantic-admission `required-1` reached `Published`. The resulting opaque admitted-source
certificate now preflights all nine durable, seven checkpoint-WAL, and 18 applicable semantic-
admission axes before successor cleanup. Exact limits succeed, positive `required-1` limits return
typed refusal with no phase trace or mutation, and per-state structural limits use the
componentwise maximum over current and every retained historical state.

A fresh checkpoint streams the exact digest-ordered retained-union closure plus its disjoint
retention manifest directly into PREPARE and the fresh index. Every object is DATA even when an
older generation contains equal bytes; no semantic entry vector, `Vec<Par>`, element sort, or second
canonical-object body exists. The exact descriptor carries current, retained-union, and checkpoint
DATA object counts and canonical bytes. Its frozen length is 216 bytes; checked formulas derive the
PREPARE extent, fresh index tail, COMMIT address, and pack tail from that one admitted inventory.
COMMIT relationally binds the PREPARE receipt, descriptor, index authority, predecessor terminal,
store, sequence, and physical addresses. Successful publication synchronizes PREPARE, index,
COMMIT, artifact directory, catalog file, and catalog directory in the verified order, then returns
authority only after ordinary restart-grade physical recovery and profile-typed semantic
readmission reproduce the same state and inventory.

All traversal remains iterative and streaming. Native stack is constant in trie depth, logical path
length, retained-state depth, and object count. Ordinary recovery retains one
`PathMap<ObjectIndexRecordV1>` for distinct DATA objects and constant replay state; index repair
pre-admits its two WAL passes, verifies the installed index directly, and constructs no second trie.
Resource retention is proportional only to authenticated inventories and explicitly bounded work
certificates, never to an artificial traversal-depth ceiling.

The parallel gate exposed a lifecycle refinement that isolated tests had hidden. A process spawn may
briefly duplicate the writer-lock open file description before close-on-exec. Closing only the
Rust lease descriptor therefore allowed the duplicate to retain the OS lock beyond the affine
lifetime. A deterministic duplicated-descriptor control was red before the repair.
`DurableWriterLeaseV1::drop` now explicitly unlocks the shared open file description before closing
its own descriptor, making the formal no-gap/no-clone authority invariant executable even across
that spawn window. The control is green and the formerly intermittent publication tests pass in the
full parallel suite.

The final `rspace_plus_plus` library gate passes **392/392** in **52.20 s**. The complete package
gate passes **817/817** in **4 min 36.055 s**, with **5.4 GiB** peak resident memory inside a 10 GiB
hard cap, zero swap, and a ten-core quota. These results establish the stack, resource, publication,
and recovery refinement of the dormant backend at the verified operation-phase abstraction. They do
not yet establish the separately tracked byte-progress crash-I/O matrix for positive short writes,
zero progress, interruptions, synchronization uncertainty, or power-loss removal of unsynchronized
names. They also do not activate the backend beneath production RSpace, replace LMDB, finish
compaction/reader-safe garbage collection, provide Windows-native authority handles, or constitute
the required LMDB-versus-PathMap throughput and storage comparison.

The Rust boundary now keeps begin and seal capabilities private until their success response is

An exhaustive finite matrix executes all six operations against all three injectable boundary

### 5.60 Ownership-disjoint structural publication and two-phase PathMap teardown [SS-C33]

#### 5.60.1 Why the prefix-local result needed an ownership correction

SS-C32 correctly removed whole-store cloning from the common **new-channel** path, but a later
mixed-construction and clone/drop matrix exposed a different boundary in PathMap 0.2.2. A shallow
CoW header clone followed by destructive exact or prefix pruning did not establish a disjoint
physical node-and-value region. Depending on insertion order and compressed-node geometry, the
candidate could retain shared payload instances or disconnect a sibling that remained visible by
point lookup. Separately, `PendingDisposals` retained every detached payload until a write cursor
closed, so a bulk value update carried $`O(k)`$ live payloads for $`k`$ replacements. Those are
ownership and retained-memory defects even though the traversal itself is iterative.

Commit `c3d48beb1` proves the publication and final-owner protocols before implementation. Commit
`68534b6fc` implements the derived invariants without changing PathMap or adding a dependency.
Value-only multiplicity updates keep PathMap's intended CoW behavior: a unique anchor updates in
place, while a shared anchor detaches through `Arc::make_mut`. Structural exact/prefix deletion uses
a fresh `PathMap` allocation because none of the released clone, graft, restrict, subtract, join,
meet, ACT, or zipper operations promises a node-and-value-disjoint result after destructive prune.
**Qualified 2026-11-14:** an exhausting single-key removal from an anchor that no other version can
reach prunes in place instead, as [5.60.7](#5607-in-place-exclusive-single-key-bag-removal) describes; a shared anchor still
takes this rebuild.

#### 5.60.2 Streaming structural rebuild

The source remains immutable until publication. One read zipper visits the complete logical trie in
canonical byte preorder. The destination is a fresh guarded trie driven by one moving write zipper.
Every retained valued endpoint is cloned exactly once; every retained maximal value-free leaf is
recreated so prefix-closed topology is preserved; selected values are never cloned. Candidate
construction and endpoint-count validation complete before a removal fold can observe the source.
Only then is the root published once. If an alias retains the old root, it remains immutable; when
its final owner retires, the ordinary guarded teardown disposes its original payload instances.

**Algorithm 44 (OWNERSHIP-DISJOINT-STRUCTURAL-PUBLISH).** The pseudocode names the two authorities
explicitly: `source` remains the only authoritative root until `candidate` is complete.

```pseudocode
candidate := fresh guarded PathMap with cloned disposal policy
removed := 0

for each logical node (path, optional_value, is_leaf) in source byte preorder:
    if deletion_predicate(path):
        removed += optional_value.is_present
    else if optional_value is present:
        candidate.move_to(path)
        candidate.set(clone(optional_value))
    else if is_leaf and path is not the root:
        candidate.move_to(path)
        candidate.create_value_free_path()

assert candidate.endpoint_count = source.endpoint_count - removed
assert iterative_count(candidate) = candidate.endpoint_count
fold selected source values in the same canonical order
publish candidate exactly once
```

For $`B`$ logical source bytes and $`E`$ valued endpoints, a structural rebuild performs
$`O(B + E)`$ work and retains the fresh result plus zipper state; native stack is $`O(1)`$ in path
depth. This is intentionally distinct from a value-only mutation, which retains the unique CoW
anchor. An already-loaded channel replacement now pays for the retained Bag stream; the previously
measured SS-C32 ladder consists of distinct new channels and continues to take the prefix-rooted
in-place branch. The replacement-specific ladder reported in §5.60.4 measures this separate
structural branch rather than extrapolating from the new-channel result.

#### 5.60.3 Final-owner teardown and bounded payload retention

Final-root destruction is a two-phase pushdown automaton (PDA). Phase A visits real values in byte
preorder, removes only the value, and immediately calls the named stack-safe disposer before the
next zipper movement. Phase B begins from value-free provenance, walks topology in reverse
byte/postorder, and uses a synthetic immediate-parent barrier so each `prune_ascend` removes exactly
one logical edge. Barriers never enter the real-payload sink. Guarded mutation uses the same
immediate-disposal rule, eliminating the proportional `PendingDisposals` vector.
**Superseded 2026-11-13:** Phase B no longer installs synthetic barriers; it cuts each value-free
edge as [5.60.6](#5606-barrier-free-phase-b-of-the-final-teardown) describes, while guarded mutation keeps its barriers.

The exact endpoint count carried by `AnchorRoot` is updated by every guarded mutation gateway and
audited iteratively before a rebuilt candidate is published. Final teardown must consume that exact
count; it never invokes PathMap's depth-recursive subtree counter. A quarantined raw header remains
inside the fail-stop unwind boundary until both values and topology are empty.

The capped zero-swap verification matrix is: GuardedPathMap **28/28** (including 65,536-byte valued
and value-free lines on a 256 KiB stack, arbitrary topology, dense root, comb, clone races, and
fail-stop disposal); Bag integration **33/33**; Bag CoW publication **3/3**; DataIndex integration
**27/27**; the executable **27-invariant / 20-mutant** channel registry; and the dedicated
legacy-teardown regression. Two exact `reduce_spec` cases additionally exercise 939-byte production
datum keys with a 203-byte common prefix through Bag/DataIndex before proving Rholang guard
backtracking and arrival-order independence. These peaks include compilation and are resource envelopes, not
algorithmic heap measurements: 85.1 MiB, 928.7 MiB, 1.8 GiB, 82.7 MiB, 81.8 MiB, and 86.4 MiB,
respectively, with zero swap.

#### 5.60.4 Result boundary

SS-C33 closes native-stack safety, exact payload conservation, sibling preservation, candidate
ownership disjointness, and the retained detached-payload slope. Five-point geometric measurement
accepts the predicted linear scaling class for both remaining mechanisms: loaded-channel
replacement has fitted exponent **0.999250304** with 95% confidence interval
**[0.996032204, 1.002468403]**, while value-free-line, valued-comb, dense-fixed-width, and
realistic-key final teardown have exponents **0.957847144**, **0.989113725**, **0.985569487**, and
**0.984322909**, respectively. All one hundred teardown observations preserve exact disposal.
Absolute replacement latency remains provisional because unrelated Rust work was active, although
the host retained approximately 55–66% aggregate idle capacity.

Headless AMD uProf attributes final-teardown CPU time to PathMap sharing checks, zipper navigation,
`AnchorRoot::drop`, pruning, and compressed-line splitting. Headless Heaptrack records 187,109
allocation calls, of which 177,403 are temporary; 181,708 line-list split allocations arise under
the synthetic immediate-parent barriers for the realistic 256-endpoint shape. Peak profiler heap is
386.49 KiB, so this is linear temporary churn rather than a retained-memory slope. The local PDA is
therefore correct, fixed-stack, time-linear, and retained-space bounded, but it is not
allocation-optimal. Removing its barriers would let PathMap detach a recursively dropped physical
subtrie, so PMU-005 now requests an intrinsic iterative destructor or nonallocating consuming
physical-node drain rather than a local workaround or fork. Full methods, medians, confidence
intervals, profile qualifications, caps, artifact hashes, and the idle-host evidence boundary are
recorded in
[`measurements/guarded-pathmap-final-teardown-and-loaded-replacement-2026-09-01.md`](measurements/guarded-pathmap-final-teardown-and-loaded-replacement-2026-09-01.md).
The barrier-free cut of [5.60.6](#5606-barrier-free-phase-b-of-the-final-teardown) (2026-11-13) answers this objection with
PathMap 0.3.4's public interface and without a fork: it never lets `prune_ascend` climb past the
immediate parent, and each `remove_branches(false)` detaches at most two nested nodes.

No Rholang value, datum identity, multiplicity, candidate order, matcher result, binding,
protobuf/bincode/EPM1/RMP2 byte, hash, COMM schedule, compute/storage charge, PathMap algebra,
accepted program, or parallel execution order changes.
