#### 5.60.6 Barrier-free Phase B of the final teardown

**2026-11-13 runtime change, bug 6441, remedy R2a.** This change supersedes the barrier step of
Phase B in [5.60.3](#5603-final-owner-teardown-and-bounded-payload-retention) and answers the
objection recorded in [5.60.4](#5604-result-boundary). Only the final teardown changes: guarded
mutation, whose live removal path (`remove_leaf_with_floor` and its barrier functions) still
installs synthetic barriers, is untouched.

**Why.** Write $`A_{\mathrm{drop}}(x)`$ for the allocation calls of a measured run $`x`$ whose call
stack contains a final-teardown frame, as counted by Heaptrack, and $`N_{\mathrm{split}}(x)`$ for
the part of them whose stack also contains PathMap's compressed-key split. The
[measurement record of 2026-11-12](measurements/guarded-pathmap-final-teardown-pathmap-0.3.4-2026-11-12.md)
found $`A_{\mathrm{drop}}`$ of 184,489 calls at the realistic 256-endpoint coordinate and 32,489 at
the 16,384-byte value-free line, of which 182,623 and 31,984 were splits: to store each synthetic
barrier, PathMap splits the compressed key that passes through the barrier's position. The
[remedy study](guarded-pathmap-teardown-allocation-remedy-study.md) (commit `b131e935a`) found
that PathMap 0.3.4's public interface already removes one edge without writing any value.

**Terms.** A *logical edge* is one byte of one path, counted once however many paths share it. A
*run* is one ascent of Phase B from the rightmost childless value-free leaf $`L = P\,b`$ (the path
of its parent $`P`$ followed by the byte $`b`$) towards the root. The run's *stopping parent* is the
first ancestor that is the zipper root, holds a value, or has more than one child (a *fork*).
Because a run starts at the rightmost leaf, every other child of its parent is a left sibling.

**Algorithm 5.60.6 (BARRIER-FREE-PHASE-B).** One run is the function
`cut_value_free_leaf_and_bubble` in
[`guarded_pathmap.rs`](../../../rspace++/src/rspace/guarded_pathmap.rs); Phase B repeats runs
until the root has no child, then reports the removed edges to the observer:

```pseudocode
input:  a write zipper z at the root of a value-free trie
output: the empty trie; one pruned(1) observer event per removed logical edge

cuts <- 0
loop
    descend z to the rightmost childless leaf
    if z is at the root and the root has no child then stop
    loop                                            -- one run
        if z is at the root then end the run
        b <- last byte of z's path; ascend one byte  -- z is at the parent P
        if P is the root or holds a value or has more than one child then
            descend back to P b; prune_ascend       -- removes exactly the byte b
            cuts <- cuts + 1; end the run
        remove_branches(prune = false) at P         -- detaches only the edge to P b
        cuts <- cuts + 1                            -- P is now a childless leaf
report pruned(1) to the observer cuts times
```

At a parent that does not stop the run, `remove_branches(false)` detaches the one child edge and
leaves the parent as the next childless leaf, so the run continues one edge higher. At the
stopping parent, `prune_ascend` from the leaf removes the run's last edge: PathMap's pruning climbs
only to the first ancestor that is the root, holds a value or has another branch, and here that
ancestor is the parent itself. Phase B starts from value-free provenance, so the value test never
fires there; it is kept so that the function never cuts below a valued parent.

**Contract.** In the table below, the first column names an observer callback or a barrier-provider
call, and the other two columns give how many times the final teardown of a value-free trie with
$`T`$ logical edges makes it before and after this change.

| Callback or call | Before 2026-11-13 | From 2026-11-13 |
|---|---|---|
| observer `installed_barrier` | once per synthetic barrier written | never; the callback no longer exists |
| observer `pruned(1)` | $`T`$ times | $`T`$ times |
| observer `removed_barrier` | once per synthetic barrier retired | never; the callback no longer exists |
| provider manufacture and retirement | once each per synthetic barrier | never |

Phase A, the signature of `retire_pathmap` and every value type's barrier interface are
unchanged, and PathMap is neither patched nor forked.

**Example.** The trie whose only path is the two bytes 1 and 2, holding one value, is torn down as
follows; it is the trie of the guard's exact-order unit test.

```text
 after Phase A            after cut 1:                    after cut 2:
 (value-free)             remove_branches(false) at [1]   prune_ascend from [1]

     root                     root                            root
      │ 1                      │ 1                            (no child)
     [1]                      [1]
      │ 2
    [1, 2]
```

Legend: a node is written as its path in brackets, and each edge is labelled with the byte it
consumes. Cut 1 is taken at the parent [1], which is not the root, holds no value and has one
child. Cut 2 is taken from the leaf [1], whose parent is the root, so the run ends; the root then
has no child and Phase B stops. The observer receives `removed_value` from Phase A and then
`pruned(1)` twice.

**Why the cut is bounded.** Write $`D`$ for the nesting depth of a drop (the number of node
destructors active at once while a detached part is dropped), $`f`$ and $`c_0`$ for the native stack
of PathMap's recursive destructor per nested node and in its constant part, $`S_{\mathrm{iter}}`$
for the stack of its iterative destructor path, and $`S_{\mathrm{nav}}`$ for the constant stack of
the zipper calls. The study's Lemma 1 shows that at a value-free parent with exactly one child,
whose child is a childless value-free leaf, exactly one slot or cell of the focus node carries
the edge. Its Lemma 2 shows that `remove_branches(false)` there allocates no node beyond a
copy-on-write clone, leaves the parent as a childless value-free leaf and drops a part with
$`D \le 2`$. Its Lemma 3 shows that `prune_ascend` below a root or forking parent removes exactly
the byte $`b`$ and drops a part with $`D \le 1`$. Its Theorem 1 combines them: Phase B empties a
value-free trie of $`T`$ logical edges in exactly $`T`$ cuts, and every cut needs at most

```math
S_{(e)} \le S_{\mathrm{nav}} + \max\left(2f + c_0,\ S_{\mathrm{iter}}\right)
```

of native stack, independent of the path depth and of $`T`$. With the study's measured release
constants ($`f = 80`$, $`c_0 = 72`$ and $`S_{\mathrm{iter}} = 144`$ bytes) the destructor's part is
at most 232 bytes per cut. The lemmas rest on premises P1 to P7 read from the PathMap 0.3.4
sources (study §2.5); they are premises about PathMap, not theorems of this repository.

**Formal evidence.** The Rocq model
[`PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v`](../../../formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v)
(commit `6fa7c8a0f`) proves `every_barrier_free_step_detaches_exactly_one_logical_edge`,
`barrier_free_step_classification` and `barrier_free_segment_installs_no_barrier`; its module
`BarrierFreeNodeRefinement` proves Lemmas 1 to 3 as `one_slot_carries_the_cut`,
`the_cut_is_bounded` and `the_stopping_cut_is_one_byte`, together with
`every_barrier_free_cut_fits_the_stack_bound`, with premises P1 to P6 stated as the hypothesis
`pathmap_premises` rather than as axioms. The Verus projection
[`pathmap_reverse_prune_teardown.rs`](../../../formal/verus/pathmap_reverse_prune_teardown.rs)
(commit `d7c330b54`) states the stopping condition as `parent_stops_the_run`, that is
`parent_is_root || parent_has_payload || left_sibling_edges != 0`, and verifies that
`executable_one_logical_edge_step` removes one edge and writes no value. The code evaluates the
same condition at the parent as `zipper.at_root() || zipper.is_val() || zipper.child_count() > 1`.
Neither model is a refinement proof of the Rust function.

**Allocation evidence (prototype).** The study measured a prototype of the same algorithm with
the record's Heaptrack protocol: $`A_{\mathrm{drop}}`$ fell from 184,489 to 1,866 calls at the
realistic coordinate (98.9 times fewer) and from 32,489 to 505 at the line coordinate (64.3 times
fewer), $`N_{\mathrm{split}}`$ fell to zero at both, and every other allocation site was unchanged
to the call. These figures describe the prototype, not this commit; re-measuring the
implementation belongs to bug 6441 (`guarded-pathmap-final-root-allocation-teardown`).

The change is confined to the final teardown of a trie that no other owner can observe: Phase A's
byte-preorder disposal is unchanged, Phase B removes the same logical edges in the same reverse
byte order, and the teardown persists, hashes and charges nothing. No Rholang value, datum
identity, multiplicity, candidate order, matcher result, protobuf/bincode/EPM1/RMP2 byte, hash,
COMM schedule, compute/storage charge or PathMap algebra changes.

#### 5.60.7 In-place exclusive single-key Bag removal

**2026-11-14 runtime change, bug 14492.** This change narrows the structural-deletion rule of
[5.60.1](#5601-why-the-prefix-local-result-needed-an-ownership-correction) in one case: removing
the last copies of one Bag endpoint from an anchor that no other version can reach. That removal
now prunes the key in place, through the guarded write cursor and the live removal path of
[5.60.3](#5603-final-owner-teardown-and-bounded-payload-retention), which keeps its synthetic
barriers. Every other structural deletion, and the same removal on a shared anchor, keeps the
ownership-disjoint rebuild of [5.60.2](#5602-streaming-structural-rebuild). The final teardown of
[5.60.6](#5606-barrier-free-phase-b-of-the-final-teardown) is unchanged, and PathMap is neither
patched nor forked.

**Why.** Write $`M`$ for the number of distinct endpoints of a Bag and $`B`$ for the logical bytes
of its trie. Before this change, a removal that took an endpoint's count to zero ran
`*self = self.subtract(&removal)` with a one-endpoint Bag `removal`. `subtract` streamed the
retained endpoints into a fresh trie through `try_from_sorted_unique`, which costs $`O(B + M)`$ by
the bound of [5.60.2](#5602-streaming-structural-rebuild), and the final drop of the replaced anchor
then drained the whole old trie. RSpace makes such removals routine: `RSpaceDataStore::remove_path`
records every removal in a pending delta, and `BagDelta::record_change` cancels it against an
earlier addition with `Bag::try_remove_many`. Each such removal costs $`\Omega(M)`$, so an
evaluation that makes $`R`$ of them on Bags of about $`M`$ endpoints spends $`\Omega(R \cdot M)`$ in
rebuilds and drains, which is quadratic when $`R`$ and $`M`$ grow together.
[PathMap journal J-259](../pathmap/pathmap-engineering-journal-2026-08-23.md#j-259--2026-11-14-an-exhausting-bag-removal-rebuilt-the-whole-bag-bug-14492)
records the diagnosis: in a release run of `system_vault_spec` alone, 52 of 57 on-CPU stack samples
(91%) were inside the drop of an `AnchorRoot`, and 41 of those 52 drops released the old Bag of a
`try_remove_many` rebuild. Three RhoSpec genesis suites exceeded their timeouts.

**Terms.** The rest of this subsection uses these terms.

- A *wrapper* is a `GuardedPathMap` value. It holds an `Arc<AnchorRoot>`, so cloning a wrapper
  (`Arc::clone`) adds one owner of the same anchor and copies nothing else.
- An *anchor* is the `AnchorRoot` behind a wrapper. It holds one raw PathMap header, the exact
  endpoint count `value_count`, the disposal policy and, from this change, the *provenance flag*
  `exclusive: AtomicBool`. Write $`w(a)`$ for the number of wrappers of anchor $`a`$, and $`f(a)`$
  for the value of its flag.
- A *header clone* is a call of `AnchorRoot::clone`. The guard reaches it only through
  [`Arc::make_mut`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Arc.html#method.make_mut) on an
  anchor with $`w(a) \ge 2`$. It copies the PathMap header, so the two anchors share every node of
  their tries until one of them writes (copy-on-write).
- An *endpoint* is one complete encoded Bag key $`k`$ with its multiplicity $`c \ge 1`$. A removal
  is *exhausting* when it removes all $`c`$ copies, so that the endpoint disappears;
  $`\lvert k \rvert`$ is the key's length in bytes.
- If $`k`$ is the root or has a child, an exhausting removal takes the value and removes no edge,
  and $`s = 0`$. Otherwise $`k`$ is a *leaf*, and its *stopping ancestor* is the longest proper
  prefix of $`k`$ that is the root, holds a value or has more than one child. The removal prunes the
  *unique suffix*, the $`s`$ bytes of $`k`$ below the stopping ancestor.
- A *logical edge* is one byte of one path, counted once however many paths share it, as in
  [5.60.6](#5606-barrier-free-phase-b-of-the-final-teardown). A *synthetic barrier* is the
  uncounted placeholder value that the live removal path writes at a value-free parent so that one
  `prune_ascend` removes exactly one logical edge
  ([5.60.3](#5603-final-owner-teardown-and-bounded-payload-retention)).

**The gate.** An anchor is *exclusive* when

```math
\mathrm{exclusive}(a) \iff w(a) = 1 \land f(a) = \mathrm{true}.
```

Each conjunct answers a different question.
[`Arc::get_mut`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Arc.html#method.get_mut) succeeds
exactly when $`w(a) = 1`$, so that no other wrapper can observe the anchor. It cannot see the
history of the nodes: after a write through one of two wrappers took a header clone, there are two
anchors, each with one wrapper, whose tries share every node. The flag records that history. It is
set only by `from_map`, which builds an anchor around `PathMap::new()`, and every header clone
clears it on both anchors, so $`f(a)`$ holds exactly when $`a`$ was built by `from_map` and no
header clone of $`a`$ has been taken since. The flag is therefore a provenance certificate, not a
sharing test. PathMap 0.3.4 itself warns, in the documentation of `ZipperConcrete::is_shared`
(`src/zipper.rs`), that "your code must never rely on the return value of `is_shared` for
correctness"; a source scan bans `is_shared` in `guarded_pathmap.rs`, `bag.rs` and
`pathmap_mutation.rs`, and `Arc::strong_count` stays banned.

The gate reads the flag with
[`AtomicBool::get_mut`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/atomic/struct.Atomic.html#method.get_mut)
(`AtomicBool` is an alias of `Atomic<bool>`), through the `&mut AnchorRoot` that only a successful
`Arc::get_mut` returns, so the read needs no atomic load. It still sees every clearing store. A
header clone stores `false` (with `Ordering::Release`) before its wrapper releases the old anchor,
and `Arc::get_mut` is a safe function that hands out `&mut` access only when no other pointer
exists. Safe Rust excludes data races
([Rustonomicon, "Data Races and Race Conditions"](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/races.html)),
so a successful `Arc::get_mut` synchronizes with the release of every other pointer. Under Rust's
memory model, which follows the C++20 rules
([`std::sync::atomic`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/atomic/index.html#memory-model-for-atomic-accesses)),
every write made through a released pointer, the clearing store included, therefore happens before
the gate's read.

**Flag lifecycle.** The table follows one anchor through every event that can change $`w`$ or
$`f`$; the figure below draws the same lifecycle as a state machine.

| Event | Code | Flag of this anchor | Flag of a new anchor | Gate afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| construction | `new_with_barrier`, which calls `from_map` with the disposer only | set | none | `Removed` |
| wrapper clone | `GuardedPathMap::clone`, an `Arc::clone` | unchanged | none | `Shared` while the clone lives, then `Removed` again |
| write with one wrapper | `Arc::make_mut` with $`w(a) = 1`$: no clone | unchanged | none | unchanged |
| write with two or more wrappers | `Arc::make_mut` with $`w(a) \ge 2`$: header clone | cleared first, with `Ordering::Release` | the copy starts cleared | `Shared` on both anchors for the rest of their lives |
| in-place removal | `remove_exclusive_endpoint` | unchanged | none | `Removed` |
| the removal empties the map | `normalize_live_empty` installs `PathMap::new()` | unchanged; never set again | none | unchanged |
| fallback rebuild | `subtract`, then `try_from_sorted_unique` and `new_with_barrier` | the replaced anchor loses the subject's wrapper | set | `Removed` for the subject |

Bug 14492's rulings fix two rows. A wrapper clone leaves the flag alone (ruling R5): the
`Arc::get_mut` conjunct already refuses while the clone lives, so a short-lived read-only clone
does not disable the in-place path after it is dropped. `normalize_live_empty` never sets the flag
again (ruling R6), because only `from_map` and a rebuild establish provenance. A cleared flag stays
cleared even after the other version is dropped: the anchor cannot tell whether that version still
shares its nodes, and the next fallback rebuild gives the Bag a fresh exclusive anchor.

![The provenance flag of one anchor: set by construction, cleared on both anchors by a header clone, never set again; a wrapper clone only makes the gate refuse while it lives](figures/anchor-exclusive-flag-lifecycle.svg)

**The algorithm.** The Bag part is the private `Bag::remove_exhausted` in
[`bag.rs`](../../../rspace++/src/rspace/bag.rs), called by `remove_many` and `try_remove_many` when a
removal exhausts its endpoint; the guard part is `GuardedPathMap::remove_exclusive_endpoint` in
[`guarded_pathmap.rs`](../../../rspace++/src/rspace/guarded_pathmap.rs), which returns
`ExclusiveRemoval::Removed` or `ExclusiveRemoval::Shared`. As elsewhere in this report, the
algorithm is in Knuth's literate style [[Knuth 1984](#ref-knuth1984)]: each named chunk, written
`⟨name⟩`, is defined once after the sign $`\equiv`$ and then used by its name, and the variable `bag`
is the Bag being changed. The figure after the walk-through draws the whole flow.

**Algorithm 5.60.7 (EXCLUSIVE-SINGLE-KEY-REMOVAL).** *Remove all $`c`$ copies of endpoint $`k`$
from a Bag: in place on an exclusive anchor, by the unchanged rebuild otherwise.*

```pseudocode
⟨Remove all c copies of endpoint k from bag⟩ ≡              ── remove_many, try_remove_many
    ⟨Step 0: preflight⟩
    case bag.entries.remove_exclusive_endpoint(k) of
        Removed ⇒ ⟨Step 7: update the Bag's metrics⟩
        Shared  ⇒ ⟨Fallback: rebuild bag without k⟩

⟨Step 0: preflight⟩ ≡                                       ── the only step that can fail
    c ← bag.entries.get(k)        or return Err(InsufficientMultiplicity)
    next ← c − amount             or return Err(InsufficientMultiplicity)
    if next > 0 then write next at k; return Ok(next)       ── not exhausting
    ── bag is unmodified up to here; no later step returns an error

remove_exclusive_endpoint(k) ≡                              ── GuardedPathMap
    ⟨Step 1: the gate⟩
    ⟨Step 2: the fail-stop boundary around steps 3 to 6⟩
    return Removed

⟨Step 1: the gate⟩ ≡
    exclusive ← case Arc::get_mut(anchor) of
                    Some(a) ⇒ a.exclusive.get_mut()         ── no atomic load
                    None    ⇒ false                         ── another wrapper lives
    if ¬exclusive then return Shared                        ── nothing was touched

⟨Step 2: the fail-stop boundary around steps 3 to 6⟩ ≡
    outcome ← catch_unwind(⟨Steps 3 to 6: prune k in place⟩)
    if outcome is a panic then abort the process            ── ruling R1

⟨Steps 3 to 6: prune k in place⟩ ≡
    with_write_cursor(cursor ⇒                              ── step 3
        cursor.move_to_existing_value(k)                    ── step 4
        removed ← cursor.remove_val_and_prune()             ── step 5
        assert removed)
    ── with_write_cursor ends with normalize_live_empty        step 6

⟨Step 5: remove_val_and_prune at k⟩ ≡                       ── NativePathCursor
    if k is the root or k has a child then
        take k's value; value_count ← value_count − 1; dispose the value
    else
        remove_leaf_with_floor(k, floor = 0)

remove_leaf_with_floor(k, floor) ≡                          ── one logical edge per iteration
    carried ← the real value at k
    loop
        ascend one byte to the parent q
        stop_here ← depth(q) = floor ∨ q holds a real value ∨ q has more than one child
        if q holds no real value then write a synthetic barrier at q
        descend back to the child
        remove the child's carried payload and its edge:
            a real value: counted out of value_count, taken with pruning, disposed
            a barrier:    discarded, then prune_ascend
        ── the value or barrier at q stops the pruning after exactly one logical edge
        if stop_here then
            retire the barrier at q, if this iteration wrote one; stop
        carried ← the barrier at q                          ── q is now a childless leaf

⟨Step 7: update the Bag's metrics⟩ ≡
    bag.distinct_len ← bag.distinct_len − 1
    bag.exact_cardinality ← bag.exact_cardinality − c

⟨Fallback: rebuild bag without k⟩ ≡                         ── unchanged: 5.60.2
    removal ← the Bag {k ↦ c}
    bag ← bag.subtract(removal)                             ── a fresh anchor, flag set
```

*Step 0* is the existing preflight. `try_remove_many` refuses a request larger than the count, and
`remove_many` clamps it; both reach `remove_exhausted` only when the request takes the whole count,
so the endpoint exists and holds $`c`$. *Step 1* is the gate above: when it answers `Shared`, the
guard has not touched the anchor, and the Bag takes the fallback. *Step 2* wraps everything that
mutates the trie in `catch_unwind` and aborts the process on a panic, the same fail-stop rule that
`AnchorRoot::drop` already applies to the final teardown; the failure-atomicity paragraph below
gives the reason. *Step 3* opens the guard's root-origin, counted write cursor. Its `Arc::make_mut`
clones nothing, because the gate proved $`w(a) = 1`$. *Step 4* positions the cursor at $`k`$, which
step 0 proved holds a value. *Step 5* is the live removal path that guarded mutation already uses,
`NativePathCursor::remove_val_and_prune`. At the root, or at an endpoint with children, it takes
the value and removes no edge. At a leaf it runs the barrier loop of `remove_leaf_with_floor` with
floor 0. The loop decides at each parent $`q`$ whether $`q`$ stops the run *before* writing anything
there, writes a synthetic barrier at a value-free $`q`$ so that the pruning below cannot climb past
it, removes the child's payload and exactly one edge, and stops at the floor, at a real value or at
a fork, where it retires its last barrier. The removed real value is counted out of
`value_count` exactly once and goes straight to the disposal policy; a barrier is never counted and
never reaches it. `remove_val_and_prune` returns `false` only when $`k`$ holds no value, which step
0 excludes, so the assertion cannot fire on a correct preflight. *Step 6* replaces a map that the
removal emptied with `PathMap::new()`, because PathMap 0.3.4 may leave a private empty sentinel
that cannot be reopened for mutation. *Step 7* lowers the Bag's two metrics; the subtractions cannot
underflow, because step 0 saw the endpoint with count $`c`$. The *fallback* is the
`subtract` rebuild of before, unchanged.

![Exhausting single-key Bag removal: preflight, gate, the fail-stop boundary around the in-place prune with its barrier loop, and the unchanged fallback rebuild](figures/exclusive-single-key-removal.svg)

**Contract.** The table compares what the two outcomes of the gate leave behind, for a Bag of
$`M`$ endpoints and $`B`$ logical bytes from which endpoint $`k`$ with count $`c`$ is removed.

| Quantity | In place (`Removed`) | Fallback (`Shared`) |
|---|---|---|
| resident endpoints and multiplicities | every endpoint except $`k`$, unchanged | the same |
| `distinct_len`, `exact_cardinality` | lowered by 1 and by $`c`$ | recounted by the rebuild, to the same values |
| `value_count` of the guard | lowered by exactly 1 by the counted cursor | the fresh anchor's exact count |
| real values disposed during the removal | exactly one, the multiplicity of $`k`$ | none; the old anchor's final owner disposes its original values |
| synthetic barriers | as many retired as written, at most one per pruned edge, none left behind | none |
| nodes or values cloned | none | every retained endpoint once ([5.60.2](#5602-streaming-structural-rebuild)) |
| anchor | the same anchor, still exclusive | a fresh anchor with its flag set |
| work | $`O(\lvert k \rvert)`$ | $`O(B + M)`$, then the old anchor's drain at its final drop |

**Example.** A Bag holds endpoint $`[1, 2, 3]`$ with count 2 and endpoint $`[1, 4]`$ with count 1,
on an exclusive anchor. An exhausting removal of $`[1, 2, 3]`$ runs as follows.

```text
 before                        iteration 1: q = [1, 2]            iteration 2: q = [1]

      root                          root                               root
       │ 1                           │ 1                                │ 1
      [1] ──4── [1,4]=1             [1] ──4── [1,4]=1                 [1] ──4── [1,4]=1
       │ 2                           │ 2
     [1,2]                        [1,2]=β
       │ 3
   [1,2,3]=2
```

Legend: a node is written as its path in brackets, an edge is labelled with the byte it consumes,
`=n` is a real multiplicity and `=β` a synthetic barrier. Iteration 1 ascends to $`[1, 2]`$, which
is not at the floor, holds no value and has one child, so it does not stop the run; it writes a
barrier there, takes and disposes the real value 2 at $`[1, 2, 3]`$ and prunes byte 3, leaving
$`[1, 2]`$ as a childless leaf that carries the barrier. Iteration 2 ascends to $`[1]`$, which has
two children and therefore stops the run; it writes a barrier at $`[1]`$, discards the carried
barrier at $`[1, 2]`$, prunes byte 2 and retires the barrier at $`[1]`$. Two barriers were written
and two retired, one real value was disposed, $`s = 2`$ edges were removed, and the Bag's metrics
fall from 2 and 3 to 1 and 1.

**Why the bounds hold.** Write $`S`$ for the native stack, $`W`$ for the work and $`A`$ for the
allocations of one in-place removal.

- *Stack.* Steps 3 to 6 are loops over heap-backed zipper state. Each pruning step detaches one
  logical edge below a parent that holds a value or a barrier, so a detached node is childless and
  its destructor nests nothing; the formal model states this step as
  `prune_segment_is_one_logical_edge` and `prune_segment_queues_no_par_job` in
  [`PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v`](../../../formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v).
  The one real value goes to the disposal policy, which must be stack-safe by the guard's contract.
- *Work.* The preflight lookup and the cursor's descent read the $`\lvert k \rvert`$ bytes of the
  key, and the barrier loop runs once per pruned edge, $`s \le \lvert k \rvert`$ times, with a
  constant number of zipper calls each.
- *Allocations.* Each iteration writes at most one synthetic barrier, which can split one compressed
  key; apart from that, only the cursor allocates, a constant.

```math
S = O(1), \qquad W = O(\lvert k \rvert + s) = O(\lvert k \rvert), \qquad A = O(s + 1).
```

None of the three depends on $`M`$, whereas the fallback's rebuild and drain cost
$`\Theta(B + M)`$. The in-place path pays allocations for its barriers, in proportion to $`s`$,
because bug 6441 kept the live removal path's barriers when it removed those of the final teardown
([5.60.6](#5606-barrier-free-phase-b-of-the-final-teardown)). The barrier-free cut of 5.60.6 is
not reused here: its premises P1 to P7 assume a value-free trie that no other owner can observe,
and a live Bag is neither.

**Failure atomicity.** Step 0 is the only step that returns an error, and it returns before any
mutation, so `try_remove_many` leaves the Bag unchanged on every `Err`. Steps 1 to 7 return no
error. A panic inside steps 3 to 6 could stop the barrier loop with a synthetic barrier still
written at a value-free parent. If that panic unwound into the caller, the Bag would be observable
with an endpoint that it never held, and `value_count` would disagree with the trie. Step 2
therefore aborts the process (ruling R1), so no execution ever observes a stray barrier. The rule
follows the existing fail-stop boundary of `AnchorRoot::drop` in the same module, which aborts
rather than resume an unwind over a half-drained trie. The fallback assigns `*self` only after
`subtract` has built and checked its complete candidate, the publish-once rule of
[5.60.2](#5602-streaming-structural-rebuild), so a panic there leaves the old Bag intact.

**Callers.** One private function changes the behaviour of every exhausting single-key removal.

| Caller | Route | On an exclusive anchor |
|---|---|---|
| `Bag::remove_many`, `Bag::remove` (one copy) and `Bag::set_count(k, None)`, when they exhaust the endpoint | `remove_exhausted` | in place |
| `Bag::try_remove_many` that exhausts the endpoint | `remove_exhausted` | in place |
| `BagDelta::record_change`, cancelling a pending addition for `RSpaceDataStore::remove_path` and for the pending loop of `RSpaceDataStore::apply_delta` | `try_remove_many` | in place; the dominant caller in J-259's profile |
| ParBag `remove_bytes` and `try_remove_bytes` | `remove_many`, `try_remove_many` | in place |
| `RSpaceDataIndex::remove_path` | its channel Bag always has a second wrapper | always the fallback |
| `Bag::subtract`, `Bag::apply_parts`, `Bag::remove_prefix` | unchanged | the rebuild, as before |

**Why the flag is kept.** PathMap 0.3.4 would be correct without it. Its write zipper calls
`make_mut` on every node it descends through, the root included, so a destructive prune never
mutates a node that another version shares, and production already runs `remove_val_and_prune` on a
copy-on-write clone in `subtract_encoded_keys` (`models/src/rust/rhoapi_ext.rs`). The flag is kept
for four reasons:

1. On an exclusive anchor no node and no value is cloned, so CBR-075's statement that removed values
   are never cloned stays true for every value type `V`, not only for cheap multiplicities.
2. Correctness does not depend on PathMap's copy-on-write internals, which the guard does not control
   and which have changed between releases: removal correctness defect PMU-008, reproduced on
   PathMap 0.2.2, is fixed only in 0.3.4 (the
   [upstream register](../pathmap/pathmap-engineering-journal-2026-08-23.md#upstream-pathmap-integration-request-register)).
3. It is the premise `exclusive_terminal_footprint` of
   [`PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v`](../../../formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v).
4. It answers the reason that SS-C33 gave for rebuilding, kept in the comment of
   `Bag::remove_prefix`: destructive pruning may traverse compressed physical nodes that immutable
   versions share. An exclusive anchor has no such version.

The price is conservatism after a header clone. A soft checkpoint snapshots the pending deltas
through the hot store's `pending_deltas`, which clones their Bags' wrappers; the next write through
either version takes a header clone and clears both flags, and the next exhausting removal then
rebuilds once and gets a fresh exclusive anchor. That is at most one $`\Theta(B + M)`$ rebuild per
Bag per soft checkpoint or journal capture, not one per COMM: `BagDelta::record_change` never clones
its Bag.

**Formal evidence.** Two Rocq leaves precede the implementation; their commits, gate logs and
counts follow.

- Leaf `bag-exclusive-removal-provenance-model` (commit `81db4de5a`, gate log `14493-gate-20261114T142145Z.log`,
  counts 252 and 341 closed-context reports with 1 and 7 kernel checks in Rocq sections A and B) extends
  [`PathMapPhysicalOwnership.v`](../../../formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/PathMapPhysicalOwnership.v)
  with a provenance world that pairs each physical anchor with a provenance bit. Its steps are
  construction, wrapper clone and drop, header clone (both bits cleared, nodes shared), write
  through one wrapper, exclusive partial release and rebuild. `provenance_run_preserves_invariant`
  shows that every run keeps the invariant, and `exclusive_gate_implies_physical_isolation` shows
  that an anchor that passes the gate, with its bit set and one wrapper, is physically disjoint from
  every other live anchor. `exclusive_partial_release_preserves_external_images` shows that a
  release by such an anchor leaves every other anchor's image unchanged.
  `exclusive_provenance_gate_is_nonvacuous` evaluates the gate on concrete runs: it is open for a
  fresh anchor, after a wrapper drop, after a rebuild and after an in-place removal, and closed
  while a wrapper clone lives and on both anchors of a header clone, which share their nodes. The
  mutants `kill_clone_that_clears_only_the_fresh_bit`, `kill_wrapper_only_removal_gate` and
  `kill_root_only_sharing_oracle` in `PathMapPhysicalOwnershipMutants.v` refute a clone that clears
  only the copy's bit, a gate that tests only wrapper uniqueness, and a bit computed by a sharing
  oracle that looks only at the root.
- Leaf `bag-exclusive-removal-live-prune-model` (commit `4d7532fe6`, gate log `14494-gate-20261114T143241Z.log`, counts
  262 and 355 closed-context reports with 1 and 7 kernel checks in Rocq sections A and B) extends `PathMapReversePruneTeardown.v` with a live removal run made of
  `prune_segment` steps above a floor. Its theorems state that each step removes one logical edge,
  that the run stops at the floor, at a real value or at a fork, that it retires as many barriers as
  it writes and disposes exactly one real value, that it queues no `Par` job, and that it preserves
  every external image under `exclusive_terminal_footprint`; `exclusive_provenance_licenses_live_removal`
  composes the run with the provenance theorem above. Its mutants omit a barrier, ignore the floor,
  leave a barrier written, and run on an overlapping footprint.

The guarded-ownership model is unchanged (ruling R4). Its invariant `GuardInvStructuralRemovalDisjoint`,
proved by `structural_removal_uses_an_ownership_disjoint_rebuild` in
[`TwoLevelRSpaceGuardedOwnership.v`](../../../formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/TwoLevelRSpaceGuardedOwnership.v),
states that a rebuilt candidate region is disjoint from its source region, so it covers the fallback
only; the in-place path builds no candidate and is covered by the two leaves above. The scope note
of [TLRS-PROP-07](../pathmap/two-level-rspace-authority-invariant-catalog-2026-09-02.md#tlrs-prop-07--copy-on-write-and-guarded-lifecycle)
records the same division. Neither model is a refinement proof of the Rust functions.

**Test evidence.** The tests ran on exports of the committed trees; the table gives their commits,
gate logs and counts.

### 5.61 Current accepted-match publication certificate [SS-C34]

SS-C34 adds the missing formal boundary between the certified candidate-search/preparation
models and a current publication record. Formal verification precedes any runtime wiring. The
Rocq unit `formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/TwoLevelRSpaceCurrentPublication.v` models one
`CurrentAcceptedProposal` whose requested channel vector and selected ordinal values are exact,
then binds `CurrentPreparedPublication` to the observed authority, the selected-candidate vector,
the typed `PreparationReady` result, the strict-subtraction/no-deletion Bag delta, and exact datum
and continuation successors. Refusal is represented as an atomic non-publication phase rather than
as a partially applied state.

The certificate is intentionally a proof boundary, not a claim that the durable backend is already
activated beneath production RSpace. It consumes the existing PathMap-native authorities and does
not reconstruct a `Vec<Par>`, sort trie entries, or introduce a second semantic representation.
The exact selected-candidate equality added in commit `ecce8a8a5` closes the remaining gap in which
PREPARE could be shown well formed without proving that it consumed the same candidate vector that
the accepted PDA selected; `129289adc` introduced the certificate and `9be709237`, `3a54fdf39`,
and `65ba2b370` provide the typed recovery, preparation, and negative-control dependencies.

Capped `coqc` and `coqchk` both pass for the registered unit with no `Admitted`, `admit`, `Abort`,
or axiom-based shortcut. The formal result proves exactness of the current publication inputs, not
filesystem durability, runtime integration, compaction, migration, or LMDB parity; those remain
separate gates in pgmcp (6361/6362, 5684, and 5688/6189). No Rholang value, PathMap topology,
protobuf/bincode byte, hash, COMM schedule, or accounting rule changes in this certificate.

### 5.62 Exact current-publication authority closure [SS-C35]

SS-C35 records the follow-up closure of the current-publication certificate boundary in
commit `417b2980c` (`formal(rspace): close exact current publication authority`). The model now
requires selector acceptance to identify the exact checked PREPARE input, observed pool,
catalogs, fresh arrival, exclusions, and selected vector; derives datum successors through the
partition-refining `PreparedRSpaceDelta`; and validates continuation successors through the exact
capability and boundary APIs. Data, continuations, cache invalidation, and generation counters
are published as one typed state transition, with the phase sequence
`Proposed → StatePublished → CommObserved`.

The refusal branch is closed as well: refusal requires the absence of every valid publication
certificate and preserves state, COMM visibility, and logical/datum/durable publication counts.
This is a formal-only strengthening of the authority boundary. It introduces no native recursive
traversal, runtime stack growth, PathMap representation change, byte/hash/COMM/accounting change,
or filesystem-durability claim. Therefore the existing stack-safety conclusion remains valid while
the previously open publication-authority correspondence is no longer left implicit.

Verification evidence: capped `coqc` and `coqchk` for
`formal/rocq/stack_safe_pda/theories/TwoLevelRSpaceCurrentPublication.v` completed successfully;
seven capstones closed under the global context, the module check succeeded, and no `Admitted`,
`admit`, `Abort`, or axiom shortcut was used. Runtime integration, durable persistence,
compaction, migration, and LMDB parity remain separate campaign gates.

### 5.63 Fixed-delta trusted commit scaling [SS-C36]

SS-C36 records the preregistered measurement of what one trusted commit costs as the current state
and the retained history grow (pgmcp experiment 446, task 7929). A trusted commit seals a mutation,
binds it under an exact trusted policy, prepares it and publishes it with no physical recovery and
no cold admission, so its work should depend on the keys that it changes, not on the $`N`$ keys of
the current state or the $`H`$ retained states. SS-C36 is a scaling measurement and makes **no stack
claim**: it measures time, allocations, I/O, resident memory and metadata bytes, not native stack
depth, and it converts no traversal.

The cost audit, the fixture, the oracles, the harness and the gates are defined in the invariant
catalog's [fixed-delta trusted commit scaling section](../pathmap/generation-checkpoint-invariant-catalog-2026-08-28.md#fixed-delta-trusted-commit-scaling-2026-10-29).
Every value below is **MEASURED (q)**, quoted from the committed
[measurement record](measurements/rspace-fixed-delta-scaling-2026-11-03.md) and its [analysis](measurements/rspace-fixed-delta-scaling-2026-11-03-analysis.json),
[process summary](measurements/rspace-fixed-delta-scaling-2026-11-03-process-summary.tsv), [verify records](measurements/rspace-fixed-delta-scaling-2026-11-03-verify.tsv) and
[artifact manifest](measurements/rspace-fixed-delta-scaling-2026-11-03-manifest.json). The raw populations are the pgmcp artifacts that Appendix B
lists.

The decision population, `decision-20261101T101751Z`, was collected at commit `941ff07d` on one
pinned CPU and ended on 2026-11-03. It has 21 cells, each with two verify runs and 31 decision time
processes. Axis U grows the current state ($`N = 2^{10}`$ to $`2^{18}`$ keys at $`H = 2^{10}`$),
axis R grows the retained history ($`H = 2^{8}`$ to $`2^{16}`$ states at $`N = 2^{12}`$), axes D and
L grow the replaced delta and the deleted group, and axis E measures physical eviction. Each
exponent is the stratified log-log slope, written as the estimate with its 95% interval in brackets.

Result 483 of experiment 446, decided on 2026-11-08, accepts its one hypothesis, H1: the larger
upper 95% bound of the two thread CPU exponents is 0.2086, against the threshold 0.25. The task's
preregistered rule also requires a qualified decision population, G1 to G9 and every control
detected. The population is qualified and all four negative controls were detected, but gate G4
fails on allocated bytes, so the rule is not met: the analysis reports `qualified` as `true` and
`accepted` as `false`.

| Gate | Verdict | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| H1, thread CPU | pass | U 0.1964 [0.1881, 0.2086]; R 0.1363 [0.1333, 0.1395]; bound 0.25 |
| G1, exact work | pass | 2 verify runs per cell, 0 problems |
| G2, determinism | pass | the verify runs agree on all 27 compared fields; 0 time-chain mismatches |
| G3, wall time | pass | U 0.1586 [0.1508, 0.1699]; R 0.1098 [0.1059, 0.1138]; bound 0.25 |
| G4, allocation count | pass | U 0.1091 [0.1050, 0.1130]; R 0.0529 [0.0479, 0.0576]; bound 0.25 |
| G4, allocated bytes | **fail** | U 0.4130 [0.4086, 0.4174]; R 0.3186 [0.3137, 0.3234]; bound 0.25 |
| G5, I/O | pass | largest upper bound over `syscr`, `syscw`, `rchar` and `wchar`, across both verify runs: 0.0575; bound 0.25 |
| G6, resident memory | pass | largest stratum's median minus the smallest's. U: $`-315{,}392`$ B, upper 97.5% bound $`-151{,}552`$ B. R: 700,416 B, upper 97.5% bound 757,760 B. Bound 1 MiB; no swap and no out-of-memory kill |

$`c^*`$, the smallest charge per key or per state that would lift H1's bound above 0.25, is
1.4142 ns per key on U and 16 ns per state on R.

The pilot forecast the G4 miss (pgmcp artifact 1178, observation O2; interval [0.380, 0.390] on U).
Hypothesis H-O2 attributes the bytes to copy-on-write copies of the widening 256-way level-1 nodes
of the reachability ledger's PathMap, about $`72 \min(\ell / 256, 256)`$ bytes per copied node for
a ledger of $`\ell`$ digests. The model matched the pilot's measured bind bytes to within 15%. The
section 5.9 diagnostics, run on the pilot's fixtures, confirm the mechanism on axis U: heaptrack
attributes 93.2%, 97.9% and 99.41% of the bind bytes at $`2^{10}`$, $`2^{14}`$ and $`2^{18}`$ keys
to `run_ledger_trial`, and its bind totals equal the verify run's counter exactly (pgmcp artifacts
1277 and 1281). The refined width model's predictions, registered before the largest trace was
read, hold. Heaptrack ran on axis U only, so axis R has the model's prediction and no attribution.
The heaptrack, strace and uProf outputs are artifact 1303, and the strace and uProf outcome is
artifact 1304. Allocation counts stay logarithmic and thread CPU and wall time pass, so this is a
cost in copied bytes per touched node, not extra allocations and not a correctness failure. The
defect is bug item `rspace-ledger-trial-cow-allocation-growth` (pgmcp item 13988), which holds the
consensus-change assessment.

The measurement does not claim the following.

- It holds for one host and one core.
- The binary is the release library test binary, which still contains the `cfg(test)` hooks and a
  toggled counting allocator, not a production build.
- The keys are data-only: each is a datum on its own channel.
- The history shares the current roots: each historical state differs from the current one only by
  its legacy root.
- fsync was measured on one filesystem, ext4.
- It makes no power-loss claim and no concurrency claim.
- It is not the LMDB verdict (task 5693). It measures no semantic eviction, because no eviction
  policy exists under keep-all retention, and axis E reclaims only physical files. It activates
  nothing (task 7931).
- $`c^*`$ bounds only what the timing gate excludes by itself: an extra cost per key or per state
  below $`c^*`$ would pass H1.

Two pre-existing gaps are noted and not fixed here: the register of section 0 has no SS-C34 or
SS-C35 rows, and the table of contents has no entries for 5.59 to 5.62.

## 6. Discussion

### 6.1 Why the explicit-worklist shape, and why it is *smaller* than what it replaces

Every conversion in §5 is the same transformation: make the continuation a **first-class value** and drive it with a loop [[Reynolds 1972](#ref-reynolds1972); [Ager et al. 2003](#ref-ager2003)]. The choice among the family's variants was made per traversal, and the discriminating question each time was *what does the resumption actually need to remember?*

| traversal shape | driver shape | why |
|---|---|---|
| pre-order into a contiguous buffer (encoder) | **op stack only, no value stack** | the output *is* the accumulator, so nothing needs parking — cf. [[Cheney 1970](#ref-cheney1970)] |
| bottom-up reassembly (decoder, substitution, sorter) | **work stack + value stack(s)** | a parent cannot be constructed until its children exist |
| post-order fold with *interleaved* checks (expression evaluator) | **work stack + value stack + an `Extract` continuation** | error **position** is observable, so per-operand checks must fire between siblings (§5.2.1) |
| a `Par` spine with a left-biased search (`into_source_process`) | **work stack, push RIGHT before LEFT** | reproduce the `.or_else` order exactly |
| a discard (ingress, teardown) | **worklist, no reconstruction at all** (`dismantle`) | nothing reads the value; only the frees are reordered |

★ **The counter-intuitive empirical result is that the heap cost per level is far *below* the stack cost it replaces** — $`5.1\times`$ for the encoder and $`42.3\times`$ for the decoder (§5.3.4). The explanation is §5.1.1's `gdb` attribution: a compiler-laid-out frame for a 40-arm `match` reserves slots for **every** arm's live locals and does not overlap mutually exclusive arms at `-O0`, whereas a work item is a hand-designed 32-byte `enum`. Trampolining is usually presented as trading space for safety; here it bought both, and the reason is that the thing it replaced was *fat*, not that the thing it introduced is *thin*.

### 6.2 Why the SCC is the unit of conversion

Three independent instances say the same thing.

* **Substitution**: converting a subset would have left the cycle intact.
* **Lowering** (§5.6.1): the reproducer's cycle passes through **twelve `core::iter` adapter monomorphisations**; the 18 direct self-call sites are *not* the component, and converting them would have left the reproducer exactly as it was.
* **The sorter** (§5.1.4): converting `sort_match` alone would have left `compare_score` $`\Theta(d)`$ **and the gate would still have passed**, because a linear chain sorts as a one-element vector on which `sort_by` performs zero comparisons.

$`\Rightarrow`$ **Scope by Tarjan, not by intuition**, and — §5.1.4 again — remember that a Tarjan run over the *schema* cannot see a recursive Rust type that is not a schema message.

### 6.3 Neutrality is the hard part, not the driver

Every one of these traversals is on a consensus-visible path. The drivers were the easy half; the expensive half was proving that nothing observable moved.

The obligations differ by traversal and were derived per traversal rather than assumed:

* **Substitution** is cost-neutral **by construction**: `substitute_and_charge` charges `encoded_len()` of the **result**, once, *outside* the recursion, and the SCC contains **zero** `reserve_*`/`Cost::` calls — asserted mechanically over all 97 corpus cases, not left as prose.
* **The sorter** takes no metering handle, which makes the *cost* obligation vacuous and therefore makes the **result** obligation the whole obligation: `cost_accounting/sig.rs` signs `sort_match(&par).term.encode_to_vec()`, so **a one-element reordering is a fork**. `sort_by` is kept and `sort_unstable_by` refused, because the comparator returns `Equal` for distinct terms with equal scores and an unstable sort would be free to reorder them.
* **The codecs** owe *byte identity* on the write side and *language identity* — including the `Err` half — on the read side.
* **The async driver** owes COMM order, checked by a differential on the ordered `(BillableKind, weight)` trace, not on a final state.

★ **`encoded_len` is the one member for which neutrality cannot be inferred from control flow**, because **its return value *is* the charge**. At `64a5d2bc`, before the generated `prost::Message` family landed, that left `subst_and_charge` at 146 B/level after a $`19.5\times`$ improvement. The final schema-generated implementation delegates `encoded_len` to the memoized bottom-up protobuf PDA and is checked against both the recursive oracle and emitted byte length. The live `subst_and_charge` ladder is therefore **0 B/level**; 146 is an intermediate historical measurement, not a residual.

### 6.4 ★ The write/read asymmetry — one section, because it is one class

The campaign kept re-discovering one shape:

> A `Par` is **written by an unbounded encoder** and later **read by a bounded decoder**, with the two ends on different paths, different processes, or different times.

**Both halves matter**, and that is not pedantry: the **bincode** wire is iterative and depth-unlimited in *both* directions, measured flat from depth 4 to 4,096, and is therefore **not in the class** — which is why the cold store does not appear in the registry at all.

Four independent instances (**DERIVED**, `rholang/tests/par_read_ceiling_site_registry.rs:1-11`):

| # | where | shape |
|---|---|---|
| **#120** | the audit's §7.3 | a term can be built, reduced and serialised but **not read back** |
| **#129** | `output_value` | play accepts a depth-34 payload; replay refuses it |
| **#130** | the trie's value slot | `decode_trie_path` is not total on `encode_trie_path`'s image |
| **#4** | `EPathMap`'s own prost wire, tag 8 | a map encodes at entry depth 34 and refuses to decode |

**#129 was downgraded by measurement, and that is a result.** The claim under test was *"a proposer-controlled consensus divergence"*, resting on a fixture that **spliced** a depth-34 `Par` into a recorded log — and that fixture's own header said splicing proves the decode asymmetry and *not* reachability. **Nobody had measured the write side.** Driving all seven reachable non-deterministic operations through real deploys on a real runtime (**MEASURED (q)**, `80f5e5d3`):

```text
rho:ai:gpt4 / dalle3 / textToAudio    depth 0
rho:ollama:chat / generate            depth 0
rho:ollama:models                     depth 1   ← the deepest
rho:io:grpcTell                       depth 0
rho:chroma:…:query (compiled out)     depth 2   recorded, not driven
```

Read ceiling 33; **tightest margin 31 levels**. $`\Rightarrow`$ **#129 is LATENT, not live.**

★ **And the defect that *is* real is not the one in the title.** The previous guard was a *sentence* — "all eight of those operations' return constructions were read" — with a hand-listed denominator. Add a ninth operation and the sentence stays grammatical, the fixture stays green, and the block-killing behaviour is live with no compile error anywhere. The denominator is now `non_deterministic_ops()` itself, read from production at run time.

**A second axis nobody had enumerated (`0e0f9719`).** Everything above concerns **depth**. `EMinus { Par p1 = 1; }` is proto3, so the field is optional **on the wire** and `prost` returns `None` for an absent one **without error**. An absent required child is therefore not something `Par::decode` *refuses*; it is something `Par::decode` **returns**. **Ten bytes** — `[2a 08 52 06 12 04 2a 02 10 04]` — are accepted by `Par::decode` and fault four independent consumers: `has_locally_free.rs` (94 sites), `spatial_matcher.rs` (55), `par_map_type_mapper.rs` (1), and the FFI (foreign function interface) rows. The disposition is settled once: an absent required child is an **internal invariant violation**, not a decidable negative, so the sites assert (`.expect`) and the fix belongs at the boundary admitting foreign bytes — because `spatial_match` returns `Option<()>`, whose inhabitants are *matched* and *did not match*, and answering `None` would make a malformed term indistinguishable from a well-formed non-matching one.

⚠ **Reachability of that axis came out split**, and is reported split: the first fault is the normaliser's own path, not the matcher; on the consensus path it is **LATENT for a structural reason** (on replay the tuple space is trace-driven, so the only pattern a spliced value ever meets is one that already matched a well-formed value at play time — five deploy-writable receive shapes all replay clean); and through the FFI it is **worse than a thread panic**, because the implicit non-unwinding shim **aborts**, so `catch_unwind` cannot intercept and the whole process dies. Severity is bounded only by there being **no in-tree caller**: a live public ABI (application binary interface) with no live consumer.

### 6.5 How the asymmetry was closed

Three options existed, and the campaign took the only one that changes no accepted-input set:

1. **Cap the writer** — rejected: a construction bound is consensus-visible.
2. **Uncap the reader** by raising `RECURSION_LIMIT` — rejected: prost's constant is private, and
   widening the accepted byte-string set is equally consensus-visible; worse, the recursion limit
   was also the sole guard on the attacker-controlled group-skip recursion (§8.6's closure table),
   so removing it first would have *introduced* a `SIGSEGV`.
3. **Convert the prost paths**, as the cold store was converted. **Taken and completed**: the
   generated `prost::Message` family (SS-A8) made the writer explicit-PDA, the group skipper was
   made iterative *before* the cap ceased to govern, and the generated decode PDAs read without a
   recursion ceiling — measured at depth 4,096 on a 256 KiB stack. All four historical instances in
   §6.4's table are closed: #120/#129 by the ceiling-free generated reader, #130/#4 by EPM1's
   direct trie image (PathMap report §5.2), which retired the per-key decode entirely.

What the deploy-path inventory still asserts is the build-vs-read headroom ratio; its one
transcribed constant (283, measured 274) is a recorded threat (§7.5), not a live bound — the read
ceiling it was ratioed against no longer exists.

## 7. Threats to validity

### 7.1 The observable is a proxy

`B/level` is the slope of *minimum surviving stack*, bisected to 4,096 B. It is **not** a direct measurement of frame size, and it aggregates every frame in the cycle. Two specific consequences:

* A traversal with $`B < 4096/\text{span}`$ is indistinguishable from $`B = 0`$ by this instrument. The gate's zero-slope ceiling over a 4 $`\rightarrow`$ 4,096 span is **4 B/level in integer arithmetic**, with the sloped control ~40 $`\times`$ above it — so the margin is real but finite.
* The estimator is affine-by-assumption. §5.6.3 exhibits a subject that is **flat then linear**, with a knee at depth ~256 whose mechanism is *not established*. Any subject measured only below its knee would be mis-classified, which is why the gate's ladders end at 4,096 and its width ladders at 65,536.

### 7.2 Measurement environment

* ⚠★ **The measured tree is HEAD *plus uncommitted concurrent work*, not clean HEAD.** `rholang/tests/stack_depth_gate.rs` — the instrument behind every `B/level` figure in [§5](#5-results) — carried **uncommitted modifications by a concurrent agent** at measurement time ($`+76`$ inserted, $`14`$ deleted; file mtime 11:47, i.e. before this session began; **this report modified no source file**). The binaries measured were built from that working tree. Three things bound the risk, and they are stated rather than assumed: the diff touches **zero** lines of `CONVERTED_DEPTH`, `TRIPWIRE_DEPTH` or any `assert_slope_below` call (checked by `git diff | grep -c`); it is predominantly `rustfmt`-shaped reflow plus an S0 doc block; and **the S0 run reproduced the independently recorded baseline table byte-exactly in all ten rows** ([§5.3.1](#531-the-baseline-what-had-never-been-measured)), which a perturbed instrument would be unlikely to do. $`\Rightarrow`$ The figures are treated as sound, and **a re-run at clean HEAD is the honest way to confirm it** — named here rather than glossed.
* **One machine, one microarchitecture.** All figures are Zen 3, `target-cpu=native`. Frame layouts are compiler- and target-specific; §5.5.2's finding that the *same* function is emitted at 48 B in one binary and 64 B in another (a $`1.5\times`$ spread **from register allocation alone**) is direct evidence that these constants do not transfer between builds, let alone between targets.
* ⚠ **Not at maximum frequency, and not on a quiet machine.** §4.2: core 8 at **77.2 %** of maximum boost, load average ~13 on 32 cores, concurrent agent workloads throughout. The **relative** timings of §5.4.1 are protected by within-repetition interleaving and by the non-overlap check; the **absolute** nanosecond figures are not, and should not be quoted as throughput characteristics of the hardware.
* **The settle was 302 s of *quieter*, not of *quiet*.** The $`\geq 300`$ s discipline was met arithmetically; the machine was never idle.
* ⚠ **`perf` used a software event.** See §4.4. Symbol attribution is unaffected; sampling fidelity is.
* **Heap figures are architecture-independent but allocator-dependent.** massif and DHAT observe the actual allocator; a different global allocator would move the block counts of §5.3.4 (though not the op-stack arithmetic, which is $`16{,}384 \times 32`$ regardless).

### 7.3 Workload representativeness

The throughput verdict of §5.4.1 is weighted by a **measured** distribution — 1,773 datums from five interpreter suites, 95.43 % at depth 2 — and that is far better than a uniform sample. But it is five *test* suites, not a production node, and it measures only `ListParWithRandom::stable_hash_bytes`'s datum leg. ⚠ A production workload with a different depth profile would move the verdict, and **per-shape magnitudes (depth 1…1,024, wide, map shapes) were never re-measured under the paired design** — only the blocked instrument produced them, so no per-shape re-weighting table is quotable.

The deploy ceilings of §5.5 are measured on **synthetic maximally-nested** source. That is the right shape for a *ceiling*, and the wrong shape for an average.

### 7.4 Enumeration completeness

The traversal inventory is **derived by three methods** — Tarjan over the schema, a call-graph search over 4,503 functions with an explicit trait-dispatch pass, and measurement as the discriminator of last resort — and each has a blind spot that was hit at least once:

* Tarjan over `RhoTypes.proto` **cannot see a recursive Rust type that is not a proto message**; it missed `score_tree::Tree<T>` and its five traversals (§5.1.4).
* A `#[derive]` scan **cannot see hand-written impls**; `PartialEq` and `Hash` are stripped from prost's output and written by hand, and a hand-picked list of four **already missed `Hash` once** (§5.3.1). The generated registry therefore declares itself a **lower bound**.
* A call-graph search cannot see rustc's **implicit `Drop` glue**, which has no `impl` anywhere.

$`\Rightarrow`$ **The list of $`\Theta(d)`$ traversals in this system should be read as a lower bound, not a census.** The read-ceiling registry (§5.7.8) exists for exactly this reason: it is a **scan**, so a fifth site cannot be added without someone deciding what it is.

### 7.5 DERIVED-but-not-MEASURED claims

Named, as required:

1. **Consensus neutrality of the ingress repair** (§5.5.3(a)) rests on three *read* arguments — signature over source, storage of source, re-normalisation by the proposer. Individually sufficient, jointly strong, **not executed** as an end-to-end differential.
2. **`protobuf_encoder`'s dormancy** (§5.3.5) is a mechanical `grep` over `src/` trees at one commit; it is DERIVED, and a future wiring would silently invalidate the "no stack-safety regression" reading.
3. **`RECURSION_LIMIT = 100`** is read from `prost-0.13.5/src/lib.rs:30`. The workspace `Cargo.lock` lists prost 0.12.6, 0.13.5 **and** 0.14.3; the *effective* version for `models` was not separately confirmed for this report, though the derived $`D_{\max}`$ values (33/32/31) **were** measured end-to-end by the gate and agree with the formula.
4. **The 87-member lowering component** (§5.6.1) is a Tarjan result from a script, not re-run for this report.
5. **The claim that no `codegen-backend = "cranelift"` is configured** is a grep over three file classes; a workspace-external `~/.cargo/config.toml` override was **not** checked.
6. **The attribution of the `env_get_deploy` movement** to the four intervening commits is explicitly *not* asserted (§5.9, #5).
7. ⚠ **`stack_depth_gate.rs`'s `BUILD_DEPTH_INVENTORY` carries a transcribed 283** where the measurement reads 274 — a 9-level drift inside a check whose resolution is 33 levels, so the check passes identically on both values. The gate file is out of this refactor's scope; the threat is that a transcribed figure beside a derivable one drifts silently (§5.7.1's class).
8. ⚠ **The clone-oracle gap is an instrument artefact bound, not a disagreement**: the re-emitted derive oracle read 7,021 B/level release where the historical monolithic impl read 3,254 — a 2.16× spread from inlining shape alone (§0). Neither is a live figure (the driver reads 0); the threat is that *semantic* oracles do not reproduce *frame layouts*, so oracle-vs-history deltas must never be read as regressions.

### 7.5a ⚠★ A measurement's provenance includes its BUILD OVERLAY — and this repo's overlay is deliberately untracked

**DERIVED**, `Cargo.toml:59-69`. This repository carries a `[patch]` block marked **`HELD LOCAL — DO NOT COMMIT`** pointing the `rholang-rs` parser crates at an **unpublished** local worktree commit — the one carrying `Proc::SignedTerm` / `TokenStack` / `Bind::Signed` that the `cost_accounting` normalizers require — and `Cargo.lock` is held out of git with `git update-index --skip-worktree`.

$`\Rightarrow`$ ★★ **An archived HEAD does not compile, by design.** `git archive` strips the overlay, and a sibling agent concluded *"HEAD is broken"* from exactly that. Anyone pinning a baseline for comparison must:

1. copy the held-local `Cargo.toml` into the export;
2. ⚠ note that its `path =` dependencies are **relative**, so the export must sit as a **sibling** of the target worktree or the paths must be rewritten absolute; and
3. **verify the baseline builds before attributing any figure to it.**

⚠ In `mettail-rust` the mirror hazard is worse in one respect: the build pin lives in a **harness-wipeable scratchpad** and can vanish on its own, intermittently breaking every build with no local change to explain it.

$`\Rightarrow`$ **A B/level figure is a property of (source, toolchain, profile, *overlay*).** This report's figures were taken with the overlay in place; a re-run that strips it will not reproduce them, and will fail to build rather than disagree.

**Experiments 306–309 provenance (2026-08-23).** The source base is
`c54a2354c99bd504ff42e20793ddd13972f6f49c`; the frozen control is
`0c27a7c878e1c8382197cd2c53f1493ca3270c39`. Experiment 309's release treatment binary has
SHA-256 `b5109de3bb0c79b8297745e08d7f973b8f8fa7582a4ef1ac6e581bf90c8dac76`; the control binary is
`3df98025a0cdb1c60e6fcf12a45340da447d8821919fb455de6895b1b6920e42`. The compiler is
`rustc 1.95.0-nightly (6efa357bf 2026-02-08)`, LLVM 22.1.0, targeting
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; Cargo is `1.95.0-nightly (fe2f314ae 2026-01-30)`. The host runs Linux
7.1.9 on x86-64. Immediately before the run, no Cargo or rustc process was live and physical cores
0–15 sampled approximately 95–99% idle; cores 16–23 were excluded because another process occupied
them. The experiment was pinned to CPU 1 inside an 8 GiB, zero-swap user scope. The complete raw
source hashes, overlay identity, paired analyses, pgmcp run digests, and headless Heaptrack capture
hash are the durable JSON/TSV records linked in §5.33 and Appendix B; nothing was inferred from a
later rebuild.

### 7.5b ★★ When a premise looks refuted, suspect the instrument ONCE before suspecting the claim

Three of this session's apparent refutations turned out to be instrument problems, not findings:

| apparent refutation | what it actually was |
|---|---|
| *"the subjects do not exist"* — the probe rejected all eleven names | **zsh did not word-split `$ SUBJ`**; every name arrived as one argument. The exact hazard `e72dcae8` records ("a zsh `set --` that does not word-split"), reproduced by me one session after reading it. |
| *"the generated tree is missing `ast_enums.rs`"* — the build failed outright | a **concurrent agent was regenerating** `target/generated/` at that moment. One retry, one minute later, succeeded unchanged. |
| *"`models` does not compile"* — E0425 in `sorter/sort_drive.rs` | a **concurrent agent's mid-edit** in the sibling worktree. Also fixed by retrying. |

★ And the general form of the lesson is already in the report twice — [§5.6.3](#563--a-retracted-claim--the-parser-is-not-depth-independent-1339c1e2-then-6275b0e2)'s parser read *"0 B/level"* because the ladder never cleared its own intercept, and [§5.7.3](#573-the-harness-prerequisite-that-was-totally-vacuous)'s generator quantified over **two values** for every input. Both looked like results.

$`\Rightarrow`$ **The rule adopted: a premise that looks refuted buys the instrument exactly one audit before the claim is doubted.** Cheap to apply, and it would have saved three false conclusions in this session alone. ⚠ It is *one* audit, not unlimited — the opposite failure, explaining away a real result as instrument error, is how [§5.5.2](#552--a-withdrawn-claim-reported-as-a-result)'s 84.3 B/level survived as long as it did.

### 7.6 The instrument shares the codebase it measures

The gate's fixtures build and tear down terms using `par_children::dismantle` — production code that the campaign itself introduced. A defect in `dismantle` would corrupt both the subject and the measurement. This is mitigated by the synthetic controls (§4.6, §5.7.4), which are self-contained and independent of `par_children`, and by the differential oracles, which are compiler-generated. It is not eliminated.

## 8. Residuals and future work

### 8.1 The prost network format — the historical ceiling and its closure

**Historical baseline** (**MEASURED (q)**, 2026-07-29): the prost **encoder** measured **302
B/level** release (**1,937** debug) — $`D_{\max} \approx 6{,}900`$ on a 2 MiB worker — and the
prost **decoder** **4,096 B/level** release, the most expensive traversal in the family, though
capped first by `RECURSION_LIMIT` at term depth 33/32/31 per envelope. The schema decomposes as
**57 `::prost::Message` derives and 5 `::prost::Oneof` derives, 37 messages in the one recursive
component** (**DERIVED**, re-counted from the generated `rhoapi.rs`).

**Final state**: both sides are the schema-**generated** explicit-PDA `prost::Message` family
(SS-A8, §5.12) — writer and reader flat, the read ceiling removed, and the group-skip recursion
made iterative *before* the cap ceased to govern (§8.6.2). The historical figures above are the
before-values of that conversion.

### 8.2 The derived `Drop` — the refuted direct route, and the route taken

The direct repair — hand-writing `impl Drop for Par` with an iterative body — was **refuted by
measurement rather than preference** (**MEASURED (q)**, `44535d75`): adding the impl produced
**353 diagnostics across 61 unique source lines in `models` alone** (38 struct-literal /
functional-record-update, 23 partial move, 0 destructure — the design's premise had counted
destructuring, of which there are zero), with the count a floor because cargo aborted before
checking the dependent crates. The impl was reverted and verified reverted. The refutation stands
as design evidence for why teardown went through the **generator** instead: SS-A8 emits the `Drop`
machinery with the rest of the trait family, and `par_drop` / `normalize_drop` are converted
register subjects at the anchor (144 and 144 B/level historical release slopes $`\rightarrow`$ **0**).

### 8.3 `<Par as Clone>::clone` — closed

The full history — call-site elimination as the interim strategy, the figures it retired (735 /
729 / 2,852 / 3,254), and the maintenance economics that deferred impl conversion — is §5.10.1.
Stage F-4 (`0eac9c3a`) generated the impl over `drive_with` and SS-A8 generalised it; the live
figure is **0** in both profiles, and the once-planned call-graph caller scan is moot — there is no
sloped impl left for a caller to reach.

### 8.4 The one heap measurement that remains unobtainable

§5.14 closed the heap axis for the four core conversions (matched-control Massif: 6,341.25 /
1,440.00 / 3,640.42 / 128.00 B/level). What remains is §5.9 #9: the **before/after allocation
churn** of the two early de-copying fixes (SS-A1, SS-D2), which a profile of the final
implementation alone cannot reconstruct — the pre-conversion tree no longer exists.

### 8.5 The `mettail-rust` measured-slope registry — zero measured slopes and closed wider SCC census

At the report anchor, `render` measured **3,665 / 911** and `lower_formula` measured
**4,094 / 978** B/level (debug / release), each with its own gate subject and named owner.

★ **Validation boundary eliminated.** Executing and proving the small shared production machine

**Integration closure extension (2026-08-03).** The remaining mettail integration tripwires have

Compile-time memory is recorded separately from runtime traversal memory. A clean, single-job

**Scope correction (2026-08-06; historical checkpoint).** At that date, “zero” in this subsection
